items.po_dataset_exceeds_cap_20260729T1140: DECISION INPUT for the resident-set trade, measured 2026-07-29T11:40Z, no action requested — but this one materially changes the shape of the trade, so read it before sizing anything. THE ON-DISK DATASET IS ALREADY LARGER THAN THE MEMORY CAP: data/live/lancedb = 785 MiB versus a 768 MiB cgroup limit (rag_entries.lance/data 596 MiB / 3137 fragments, _indices 145 MiB / 745 files, _versions 32 MiB, _transactions 12 MiB). Combined with the fixed ~700 MiB embedder singleton already recorded on this row at po_measured_input_20260729, the cap is being asked to hold a fixed model baseline AND the working set of a corpus that already exceeds the whole limit on its own, while the corpus grows ~103 rows/h and RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND is time-gated until it reaches ~56254 rows (~5x today). SO THE QUESTION THIS ROW OWNS IS NOT ONLY how many MiB to grant. A cap chosen to fit today loses the same argument again in weeks, because two of the three consumers grow without bound. The options worth costing are at least: (a) raise the cap against the 16GB host budget this row already owns, (b) shrink the fixed baseline (a model release path — embedder.py has none, which is the finding on FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP, or a smaller/quantised model), (c) shrink the dataset footprint so the working set is bounded (compaction and version retention — FIX-RAG-COMPACTION-DISK-AMPLIFICATION, raised to P2 this tick on this evidence). NOT ESTABLISHED, and it gates option (a): whether the charged memory is reclaimable file-backed cache or anonymous allocation. Nobody has read the container cgroup memory.stat anon/file split — see the same caveat on the CLEAN-EXIT row. If it is mostly file cache then raising the cap buys throughput, not safety, and the real fix is (b) or (c); if it is anonymous then (a) is genuinely load-bearing. Do not size a cap change before that split is measured. PO is NOT authorising a cap change or a rebuild — user-gated infra.

NEITHER OF THE ROUTER'S TWO FRAMINGS IS CORRECT. It is not 'undeployed-fix-still-pending'. It is ALSO not 'deployed-fix-does-not-work', and that distinction is the whole triage: FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP was never scoped to close this symptom — its own AC6, already quoted on this row at po_ack_retarget_20260729T1126, reads verbatim 'Does NOT claim to close the restart loop... the residual belongs to FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY'. The residual is THIS row and always was. RECURRING-BUG-ESCALATION THEREFORE DOES NOT FIRE ON THE CODE FIX — there is no 2nd occurrence of the defect it fixed; 60 min of container logs show a single clean startup at 12:17:21Z, one model load, no optimize storm, no error signature. It DOES fire on the dispatch path — see po_RECURRING_dispatch_gap_20260806T1245. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED IS ALREADY DECIDED AND UNEXECUTED: architect_review_note on this row (2026-08-06T09:03Z, brief docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-06-rag-service-memory-sizing-remediation.md) chose deploy.resources.limits.memory 768m->1g and reservations.memory 256m->512m. AS OF 12:45Z docker-compose.yml lines 165-172 still read `memory: 768m` and `memory: 256m`, and that file's last commit is 4bac2b85d dated 2026-07-28 — the decision has not been applied to a single byte. LIVE STATE AT RULING TIME: 767.3MiB/768MiB = 99.91%, RestartCount=6, StartedAt 2026-08-06T12:17:21Z, status healthy — i.e. refilled to the ceiling in ~25 min after the most recent restart. NOT gated on QA of FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP — different file, different defect, no dependency in either direction. HEADROOM INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY PO rather than inherited from the brief: `docker info` MemTotal = 7939 MiB and `docker stats --no-stream` sums 2299 MiB actual across 13 running containers, so a +256 MiB ceiling raise lands at ~2555 MiB against 7939 MiB even if fully consumed. items.po_RULING_no_naked_restart_20260806T1245: PO RULING 2026-08-06T12:45Z — an interim container restart as a stopgap is REFUSED. This is a standing disposition on this row, not a one-off, because the question keeps being asked whenever the memory figure crosses 99%. It has negative expected value. (1) It buys no safety that is not already armed: docker-compose.yml sets `restart: unless-stopped` on rag-service, so the OOM-kill path ALREADY auto-recovers — which is exactly what was observed at 08:17:30.93Z, a container start 1.6s after the die. A manual restart duplicates a mechanism that is already running. (2) It buys minutes, and that number is measured twice on this row rather than estimated: post-restart the container read 95.09% within minutes at 08:17Z, and today's 12:17:21Z restart had refilled to 99.91% by 12:42Z — roughly 25 minutes of purchased headroom. (3) It carries a real cost every time: a cold start discards the embedder singleton and reloads the ~400MB sentence-transformers model, confirmed in the container logs on every start ('Loading embedding model: ... (first load ~400MB)'), during which the service answers degraded. THE ONLY RESTART WORTH SPENDING IS THE ONE THAT CARRIES THE NEW CAP. The `docker compose up -d --no-deps rag-service` authorised at po_RULING_fix_is_deployed_dispatch_now_20260806T1245 IS a restart — it just comes back with ~270-300MiB of headroom instead of the ~0.7MiB free the container has right now. Do not spend a restart before it, and never spend one instead of it.
items.po_CORRECTION_reclamation_dip_observed_2: PO CORRECTION TO THE A-30 EVIDENCE, measured 2026-08-06T12:50-12:52Z — does NOT change the ruling above, but a future reader must not inherit the premise it corrects. THE CONTAINER DOES RECLAIM, AND IT DID SO WITHOUT A RESTART. PO sampled after writing po_RULING_fix_is_deployed_dispatch_now_20260806T1245 and found 658.5MiB/768MiB = 85.74%, held flat across five samples at 12:50:50/12:51:03/12:51:17/12:51:30/12:51:43Z, with RestartCount STILL 6 and StartedAt STILL 2026-08-06T12:17:21.934721631Z — both unchanged from the 12:42Z reading of 767.3MiB/768MiB = 99.91%. That is ~109MiB reclaimed in ~8 minutes with NO restart, NO OOM event, and no lifecycle transition of any kind. WHAT THIS CORRECTS: the A-30 discriminator verdict relayed into this tick's triage ('all samples >93% with no reclamation dip', 6 samples at 99.69-99.74%, verdict ESCALATE = genuine leak not GC sawtooth) is a SAMPLING-WINDOW ARTIFACT, not a property of the container. A dip of this size was available to observe roughly 8 minutes after the last sample the discriminator took. Note this is the OPPOSITE error class from the one already on record at feedback_a30_discriminator_crash_cliff_misscored_as_reclamation_dip, where a crash-cliff was scored AS a reclamation dip — here a real reclamation dip was MISSED because the sampling window closed before it. The discriminator is now known to err in BOTH directions on this container, so its verdicts are corroborating evidence at best and must never be the sole basis for an escalation or a stand-down. Cross-referenced on this row at po_related_detector_defect_20260806T0824, which already flagged the same script as inheriting doubt here. WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* CHANGE, and this is the load-bearing half: (1) The 08:17:28Z OOM kill is unambiguous and is not a dip-counter inference — `docker events` recorded `container oom` then `container die` exitCode=137 (SIGKILL). A container that reclaims is still a container that got killed. (2) 658.5MiB is the BEST observed state, and it leaves ~110MiB of headroom against a peak that reached 767.3MiB the same hour. The measured need on this row is ~726-750MiB resident plus a ~20MiB compaction burst; 85.74% at rest with a 99.91% peak is exactly the shape of a workload whose peak exceeds its cap. (3) The sizing decision was never derived from the dip counter — po_GATE_DISCHARGED_anon_dominant_20260729T1148 rests on a cgroup anon/file split (~95% anon, ~726MiB process-resident), which this observation leaves untouched. THE CAP RAISE 768m->1g REMAINS AUTHORISED AND URGENT. Do not read 85.74% as the pressure having passed and stand the dispatch down — that would be feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data with a friendlier number attached.

PO 2026-08-06T14:15Z — THE OPEN BRANCH QUESTION FROM po_POSTRAISE_WARNS_UNRESOLVED_20260806T1355Z IS NOW ANSWERED: BRANCH B. The 1GiB cap IS live on the running container. A SECOND CAP RAISE IS THE WRONG MOVE.

I had written that one `docker inspect` (HostConfig.Memory + StartedAt) splits deploy-gap from genuine escalation, because 97.06% of 768MiB is 745MiB while 97.06% of 1024MiB is 994MiB. That check is no longer needed to decide the branch — ARITHMETIC ALONE SETTLES IT, and the reading was already sitting in the auditor notebook:
  c58 @2026-08-06T13:36:07Z: 'Memory usage: 992.6 MiB / 1 GiB (7.4 MiB free, BELOW 40 MiB safety floor)', 'rag-service: Up 39 min (post-cap-raise to 1GiB), RestartCount=0, 96.94%'
  c57 @2026-08-06T13:18:03Z: 'rag-service: Up 17 min (post-cap-raise to 1GiB), RestartCount=0, 96.31%'
DECISIVE POINT, independent of any label the auditor attached: the container is USING 992.6 MiB. That is physically impossible under a 768 MiB cap. So the effective cap is >768MiB regardless of whether the '1 GiB' annotation is trustworthy. Cross-check: 992.6/1024 = 96.93%, which reproduces the reported 96.94% to rounding; under a 768MiB denominator the same absolute usage would read 129%. Two independent cycles agree, and the uptimes (17 min at 13:18Z, 39 min at 13:36Z) both put container recreation at ~13:00Z, immediately after cap-raise commit 2f835ec63 (13:00:35Z).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: the cap raise deployed correctly and DID NOT FIX THE PROBLEM — rag-service re-saturated a 33% larger cap within ~17 minutes of a clean start (RestartCount=0), and sat at 96-97% flat with 7.4 MiB free. That is the signature of a workload whose resident set expands to whatever it is given, not of a cap that was merely too small. FIX-RAG-EMBEDDER-IDLE-UNLOAD-PATH (BACKLOG, P2, developer) is therefore PROMOTED FROM FOLLOW-UP TO PRIMARY REMEDY, exactly as my 13:55Z carry-over specified for branch B. Recommend re-prioritising it P2->P1 on its own row when next touched by an agent that owns it.

HONEST LIMITS OF THIS EVIDENCE (do not overstate downstream): (1) these are auditor SELF-REPORT lines; the c59 'RAW-PROBE' block in the same notebook is summarised ('[13 containers all Up]'), not a real dump, so this is not raw-plane confirmation. (2) The 992.6 MiB figure is what carries the proof, NOT the '(post-cap-raise to 1GiB)' annotation and NOT the A-30 dip verdict — per this row's own po_CORRECTION_reclamation_dip_observed_20260806T1252, the A-30 discriminator has erred in BOTH directions on this container and remains corroborating-at-best. (3) A `docker inspect rag-service --format '{{.HostConfig.Memory}} {{.State.StartedAt}}'` is still worth one line at QA time to confirm HostConfig vs a live `docker update`, but it is now CONFIRMATORY, not branch-deciding.

JSON null into a non-pointer float is a documented encoding/json no-op, so the field keeps zero; `change := item.Change` then `Change: &change` takes the address of a local -> structurally never nil. mapper.go (:30-31) declares them *float64 and copies only when non-nil.

WHICH SIDE IS RIGHT: the PRIMITIVE. pkg/domain/models.go:22-23 documents `Change *float64 // nil = unavailable, 0 = genuine flat day` -- named invariant DSI-INV-1. The served path violates it today. The mapper_test cases null_change_and_pctChange_maps_to_nil_pointers / omitted_change_fields_treated_as_nil / partial_null_-_only_change_is_null encode the documented contract, not an arbitrary copy's behaviour. Reverting mapper.go to the non-pointer shape would enshrine the violation and break 3 green tests.

YOUR REMAINING WORK:
(1) Re-confirm the divergence above yourself (cheap: unmarshal the three payloads into both struct shapes, compare nil-ness). Then golden-diff EVERYTHING ELSE -- code/price scaling/source switch/empty/malformed -- and confirm those ARE byte-equivalent, so the change-pointer semantics is the ONLY intended behaviour delta.
(2) Rewire Tier1/Tier2 fetchers.go to CALL the primitive, deleting the inline duplicate (this is the actual dedup this task exists for). Collapse to one doFetch(url) per the approach field.
(3) Confirm the served Price (the *1000 scaling and source mapping) is UNCHANGED for sample tickers after rebuild -- that part must be behaviour-preserving.
(4) The change/pctChange semantics WILL change on the wire: an unavailable change flips from 0 to null. This is a deliberate DSI-INV-1 bug fix, not a silent side-effect. It is tracked as its own row -- FIX-STOCK-PRICE-VNDIRECT-DSI-INV-1-NULL-CHANGE-SERVED-AS-ZERO (P1, backlog) -- and ONE rewire closes BOTH rows. Read that row's AC-1/AC-3 before you ship: AC-1 asks you to establish empirically whether VnDirect actually sends null/omitted change live, and AC-3 requires auditing every consumer of FetchPriceResponse.Change/.ChangePercent (Go plane AND any TS/frontend JSON consumer) for a bare dereference or non-nil assumption. Do NOT bill the work twice; close both rows together.
(5) Delete or correct the false comment `// DSI-INV-1: use pointers so 0 is distinguishable from nil (unavailable)` at fetchers.go:88 and :192 -- it is false with respect to its own code.

NOTE: rebuild_required is genuinely TRUE here (already set) once fetchers.go is rewired -- served-path change to a shipped binary -- even though the tests task was rebuild_required:false.

items.title: Source-fetch-completeness audit: every IMPORTANT source pulls COMPLETE detail (no partial/stub/truncated persisted-as-complete)

items.failure_mode: A source returns a partial/reference/stub payload (missing fields, zero-volume placeholder, truncated list, silent-0-rows, single-page-of-many) and the writer persists it as if complete -> poisons served metrics.
items.generic_mandate: Every completeness check + any fix MUST be generic across ALL entities of a source (all tickers / all pages / all series) — NO per-instance allowlist (goal #2).
items.method_per_child: 1) DEFINE complete-detail (objective field/row/page invariant). 2) PROBE live fetch trigger vs def via gateway/RAW (recon-only, ops). 3) If a partial-persist gap is found -> mint a FIX in the persisting zone (dev-mcp-server for the writer). 4) done_verified = live VARIED complete data vs named-volume DB, not a constant.

items.title: Health-recheck BCTC monitor misreads idle-queue-0-running as CRASH (push-age>360min false P0)
items.desc: The analysis-agent health-recheck cron flags vn-bctc-fetch as CRASHED/UNHEALTHY (SLA breach) whenever last-push-age > 360min, but cannot distinguish a legitimately IDLE pipeline (service active+running, queue EMPTY because 9-11 watchlist tickers simply have not filed Q1-2026 yet) from an actual DOWN service. dev-team SSH RAW-verified 2026-06-19T16:20Z (report 3256): vn-bctc-fetch active(running) 8+ days, NO crash, queue legitimately empty. This monitor fires a false BCTC P0 ~every 2h, spamming health-recheck reports (~14 of reports 3244-3262). DISTINCT FROM FIX-BCTC-FRESHNESS-GATE (done_verified) which gates SERVICE health on last_success_age — that is the inverse (make gate MORE sensitive); THIS task makes the CRASH classifier require service-state + queue-depth probe before declaring crash. Same class as memory feedback_bctc_lastpush_age_misread_as_crash + feedback_false_infra_failure_corroboration_gate.
items.root_cause: Crash detector keys on last-push-age>360min alone (event-driven push age) without checking service-state (active/running) AND queue-depth. push-age is high whenever the queue is empty/idle (no filings due), which is normal off-filing-season, not a crash.
items.fix_spec: Locate the BCTC crash/SLA classifier feeding the analysis-agent health-recheck report (candidates: apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/financial-reports/bctcOverdueCheckJob.ts, scheduler/vpsProxyWatchdogJob.ts, interface/mcp/routes/fetchStatusHandler.ts). Gate the CRASH/UNHEALTHY verdict on: service-state != active/running OR (queue-depth > 0 AND last-success-age > SLA). When queue-depth == 0 AND service running == idle-waiting -> emit INFO (idle, no filings due), NEVER P0 crash. Generic: derive SLA window only over tickers with an EXPECTED-but-missing filing, not calendar age. Add a unit test: idle-queue-0-running + push-age>360min -> verdict=IDLE/INFO (not CRASH); down-service OR (queue>0 AND age>SLA) -> CRASH.
items.verification_gate: Unit: idle-queue-0-running + push-age>360min => INFO not CRASH; service-down => CRASH; queue>0 & age>SLA => CRASH. Live: next health-recheck cron tick over a running-idle vn-bctc-fetch emits NO false BCTC P0.
items.generic_mandate: Fix the classifier generically (service-state + queue-depth gate), not a vn-bctc-fetch special-case; applies to any event-driven pipeline whose push-age is idle-dependent.

(B) alerts accumulates stale UNRESOLVED rows with no resolution/cleanup/retention policy -> 829 unresolved / 205 unresolved >30d (Apr-May rows still unresolved as of 2026-06-21). Same no-GC retention family, same mcp-server zone — broadened this task from agent_signals-only to a shared DB-retention/GC cron rather than minting a duplicate alert-cleanup task (task-count conservation).] HARD CONSTRAINT for dev (BOTH tables): expires_at / triggered_at / resolved_at are ISO-TEXT ("2026-06-21 17:00:01"), so EVERY GC/retention DELETE/UPDATE and count predicate MUST use datetime(col) < datetime('now','-N days'), NEVER epoch strftime('%s',...) compare (epoch returns 0 on ISO-TEXT, silently no-ops — feedback_sqlite_iso8601_datetime_strcompare_bypass trap). items.title: get_macro_calendar serves empty events[] — MCP tool proxies the FDA-4 honest-unavailable Go stub while a complete unwired static-calendar domain service exists in mcp-server

items.desc: ROOT CAUSE: MCP tool get_macro_calendar (apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/macro/carryTools.ts:110) does an HTTP GET to the macro-indicators Go /macro-calendar endpoint (apps/macro-indicators/pkg/interface/http/handlers_calendar.go), which is the FDA-4 honest-unavailable STUB — it ALWAYS returns {events:[],status:unavailable,is_estimate:true,source_tier:4} because no live source was ever wired there. BUT a COMPLETE, usable calendar already exists UNWIRED in the same mcp-server: apps/mcp-server/src/domain/services/macro/macroCalendar.ts exports getMacroCalendar(referenceDate?,days=60) returning ~36 FOMC/GSO-CPI/GSO-GDP/Vietnam-PMI/SBV 2026 events with isPivotWindow + currentMonthIsPivotWindow + nextPivotWindow + pivotWindowWarning (pure function, NO external fetch). FIX (pick the cleaner of): (a) repoint the MCP get_macro_calendar tool at the local getMacroCalendar() domain service (drop the HTTP hop entirely — simplest, the data is local), OR (b) have the Go /macro-calendar handler serve an equivalent static schedule. Either way the served source_tier should reflect 'derived static schedule' (tier 3, as carryTools.ts already documents) NOT tier-4 unavailable. Restores the pivot_window_active signal that digest-predict + alert-commander consume.

items.title: Structural-template validator for FB posts — canonical header, verbatim disclaimer, valid hashtag block, no markdown in body
items.root_cause: 2026-06-23 daily FB post (docs/social/fb-post-2026-06-23.md) PASSED both number-gates (fb-jargon-gate.sh exit 0 AND fb-data-integrity-gate.sh exit 0) while violating the post TEMPLATE in 4 ways — caught only by router manual review. NEW DEFECT CLASS validated by NEITHER existing gate. 3rd+ consecutive day structural/prose defects slipped the number-gates.
defects: Non-canonical header: emitted '# Bài phân tích thị trường 23/6 — ...' instead of required '# Thị trường chứng khoán Việt Nam — YYYY-MM-DD'.
Invented disclaimer block instead of the verbatim standard one (must start '⚠️ Nội dung được tạo tự động bởi bot AI, chưa được kiểm chứng...').

Broken hashtag block: emitted hashtags WITH diacritics and spaces ('#ThịTrườngChứngKhoán', '#Việt Nam' — the space splits into a broken tag). Facebook hashtags cannot contain diacritics or spaces. Required = lowercase no-diacritic ASCII set (#chungkhoan #chungkhoanvietnam #vnindex ...).
Heavy markdown (## headers, ** bold, --- rules) in the body region — pastes as literal characters on Facebook.
items.fix_spec: Add a structural validator (new scripts/fb-structure-gate.sh, or a Check block in fb-data-integrity-gate.sh) that asserts: (1) canonical header line matches regex '^# Thị trường chứng khoán Việt Nam — \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$'; (2) verbatim standard disclaimer block is present; (3) hashtag block is all-lowercase ASCII, no diacritics, no spaces, and includes the mandatory 5 (#chungkhoan #chungkhoanvietnam #vnindex + the two others in the canonical set); (4) no markdown '##' / '**' / '---' inside the body region. Exit NON-ZERO on ANY miss (heed the prior fb-gate false-green class — feedback_fb_poster_gate_false_green — verify it actually exits non-zero).
items.ssot_mandate: The canonical header, verbatim disclaimer, and the mandatory hashtag set must live in ONE place (the poster flow doc docs/agents/fb-market-poster/flow/main.md, OR a small JSON the gate reads) — NEVER hardcoded twice. The validator and the poster read the SAME source.
items.generic_mandate: Validate by template-conformance assertion, generic over any daily post; no per-day hardcoding.
items.verification_gate: Feed the 2026-06-23 defective draft (or a fixture reproducing each of the 4 defects) → gate EXIT NON-ZERO citing each violation. Feed a compliant post (canonical header + verbatim disclaimer + clean ASCII hashtag block + markdown-free body) → exit 0.

items.title: system-auditor C-11 (pdf_documents) check predicate broken: queries status=done (never exists) + ISO-8601 vs datetime() strcompare bypass -> ALWAYS false-fails
items.description: C-11 (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md L478 spec table + bun:sqlite probe) is: count(*) FROM pdf_documents WHERE status='done' AND extracted_at > datetime('now','-48 hours'). RAW live probe (pdf_extractor.db, 2026-06-25T00:37Z, 42233 rows): DISTINCT status = failed(40758)/processing(1376)/success(99) -- there is NO 'done' status, so the predicate ALWAYS returns 0 and C-11 false-fails on every scan. TWO bugs: (1) status literal 'done' must be 'success' (the real terminal-OK status); (2) extracted_at on success rows is ISO-8601 with T separator (e.g. 2026-06-15T22:13:09.472421) while datetime('now','-48 hours') returns space-separated, so the string compare bypasses (feedback_sqlite_iso8601_datetime_strcompare_bypass) and even after fixing the status literal the 48h window mis-evaluates. failed/processing rows have NULL extracted_at.
items.fix_spec: Correct C-11 in BOTH the L478 spec table row AND any bun:sqlite probe block: (a) status='done' -> status='success' (verified the ONLY terminal-OK value; failed/processing are the other two). (b) Replace the ISO-8601-vs-datetime() string compare with an epoch-seconds compare so the 48h window evaluates correctly against the T-format column, e.g. WHERE status='success' AND strftime('%s',replace(extracted_at,'T',' ')) > strftime('%s','now','-48 hours'). GENERIC: no date literals. (c) C-11 is gated > 0 in the earnings window; an out-of-season 0 (Q2 filings land Jul-Aug) should be INFO not HIGH -- apply the same off-market/earnings-season-awareness pattern already prescribed for C-06 (FIX-AUDITOR-C06-OFFMARKET-RECALIBRATE).

items.title: fb-gate Check-C: negation-blind to Vietnamese 'chưa' false-blocks orderly-pullback posts + \d->[0-9] BSD-grep portability
items.lesson: L4 (2026-06-25 -0,80% orderly post FALSE-BLOCKED twice: 'chưa hoảng loạn'/'chưa phải bán tháo' counted AFFIRMATIVE — 'chưa' absent from Check-C negation-strip set)
items.desc: Check-C builds SELLOFF_AFFIRM_LINES by removing lines that match the negation set {không phải|không có|không bán|chứ không|mà không} (line ~342). 'chưa' (not yet/not) is NOT in that set, so an explicitly-negated panic statement ('lực bán chưa hoảng loạn', 'chưa phải bán tháo') survives the strip, is counted as an AFFIRMATIVE selloff claim, and on a mild day (|VN-Index|<2%, ~0 floor) FALSE-BLOCKS a correct non-panic post. FIX (1): add 'chưa' and common variants ('chưa phải','chưa từng') to the negation-stripping lexicon. FIX (2): replace `\d` with `[0-9]` in the floor-stock regex `chỉ \d mã sàn` (line ~361) — BSD grep -E on macOS treats `\d` literally; `[0-9]` is GNU/BSD portable.
items.generic_mandate: Broaden the negation lexicon generically (any 'chưa'-prefixed negation of panic language), not a one-off literal; the [0-9] portability fix applies to EVERY `\d` in the gate's grep -E patterns — audit the whole script for stray `\d` while here.

items.title: system-auditor Size-cap §4 task_board>80 predicate counts lifetime-accumulated CLOSED sprint tasks, not active WIP -> recurring false-CRITICAL doc_size_breach
items.description: docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:399 predicate `[.task_board.active_sprints[].tasks[]] | length > 80` fired CRITICAL doc_size_breach at 2026-06-26T00:31:41Z reporting 248 items. RAW status-breakdown of those 248: 242 (~97.6%) carry a TERMINAL status (163 DONE / 40 DONE-LIVE-VERIFIED / 14 done / 7 done_verified + CANCELLED/CLOSED-NO-CHANGE/CLOSED-NOT-REPRO/SUPERSEDED/DEFERRED); only ~6 are non-terminal (2 TODO, 3 BACKLOG, 1 blocked-probe5). Active WIP across ready+in_progress+qa+review = 1. active_sprints[].tasks[] is an append-only accumulation of completed sprint tasks, so this count grows without bound and the >80 gate fires CRITICAL to=po on every scan once enough sprints close. The 80-cap is meant to bound ACTIVE board size, not lifetime sprint history.
items.fix_spec: Split the §4 size-cap into two checks. (a) ACTIVE-WIP gate: count [.task_board.ready,.task_board.in_progress,.task_board.qa,.task_board.review]|map(length)|add; alert (non-CRITICAL) only when active WIP exceeds a real WIP cap. (b) ARCHIVE-DEBT trigger: when active_sprints[].tasks[] accumulation (preferably excluding terminal-status tasks) exceeds a bloat threshold, route a routine INFO/LOW signal to pm to run the existing task-archive sub-flow (docs/agents/pm/flow/task-archive.md) — NOT a CRITICAL doc_size_breach. Stop counting DONE/done_verified/CANCELLED/CLOSED/SUPERSEDED tasks toward an active-WIP cap.
items.generic_mandate: Count active-WIP lanes for WIP caps; exclude terminal-status tasks; route accumulation-bloat to the routine archive trigger at INFO/LOW severity, never CRITICAL. No hardcoded counts (read from orch-state).

items.title: cowork last_fired is bumped on spawn DISPATCH-success, not delivery proof -> a spawn that dies before writing its notebook still satisfies the cadence gate -> genuine slot misses are MASKED (matcher never re-offers)
items.description: RAW-verified 2026-06-26 from cowork-dispatcher signals (00:19Z cowork_spawn_completion + 00:22Z blind-correction) and confirmed in docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/last-fired.md Step 5b: last_fired updates for WON_SLOTS where 'won' = the run_in_background spawn handle returned (AC-P1-7-1 'last_fired written after successful spawn'), NOT delivery confirmation (notebook mtime advance / marker file). A backgrounded spawn that dispatches then dies before delivering still bumps last_fired; cowork-match-slots.js then reads the bumped stamp, sees the 4h cadence satisfied, and never re-offers the slot -> the miss is invisible. OBSERVED: news-scout-offhours 00:00 master-cron fire bumped last_fired 00:02:36Z but produced NO c108 notebook cycle (latest real c108 @ 06-25T16:04Z; both 20:00 and 00:00 slots un-run), while sibling bctc-analyst-slot-4 + market-watcher-offhours DID deliver real cycles -> gateway was up -> the news-scout spawn died before delivery. Same masking class as the prior bctc-analyst-slot-3 master-cron gap. The dispatcher only caught it via an ad-hoc marker-safe recovery spawn (which then turned out blind) — there is no SYSTEMIC delivery-confirmation gate.
items.fix_spec: ARCHITECT confirm zone split + design first (do NOT pre-commit to an approach). The hard constraint: spawns are run_in_background (fire-and-forget) so the dispatcher CANNOT synchronously await delivery within one tick. Candidate designs to evaluate: (A) DEFERRED-CONFIRM ledger — on spawn, record a pending_delivery{slot_id, dispatched_at, expected_artifact} marker and DO NOT bump last_fired; on a SUBSEQUENT tick, bump last_fired only if the slot's delivery artifact (notebook mtime > dispatched_at, or a per-slot delivery marker) advanced, else re-offer the slot (bounded retry budget to avoid thrash). (B) POST-SPAWN short delivery poll before the Step 5b write (bounded, < tick budget). (C) artifact-driven cadence — derive 'last delivered' from the slot's real delivery artifact mtime rather than a dispatch-stamped field, making last_fired advisory. Architect picks; BA decomposes into dev-ready fix_spec+files. cowork-schedule.json is _maintained_by agent-father via architect brief ONLY (never direct edit) — flow-doc + matcher changes route to dev-mcp-server / agent-father per the split.
items.generic_mandate: Cadence suppression MUST be gated on DELIVERY PROOF, not dispatch success, for ALL fire-and-forget cowork slots (not just news-scout) — a slot whose spawn dispatched but never delivered must remain due. Applies to every */4h + guaranteed slot in cowork-schedule.json. No hardcoded slot lists — derive from the schedule.
items.verification_gate: Simulate a slot whose spawn DISPATCHES successfully but produces NO delivery artifact (no notebook mtime advance / no marker) within the delivery window -> last_fired is NOT advanced (or the slot is re-offered next tick) AND the matcher re-offers it on the next cron period; a slot that DOES deliver advances last_fired exactly once and is correctly suppressed. Both behaviors covered by cowork-match-slots.test.js (or its successor). Confirm no re-fire thrash on a slow-but-eventually-delivering spawn (bounded retry).

items.title: task_claim owner_session is server-INSTANCE-scoped (pid+startupTs), not client-scoped -> concurrent clients on one mcp-server collapse to one owner identity -> re-entrant self-reclaim returns claimed:true -> mutual exclusion DEFEATED (cowork double-fire)
items.root_cause: apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/system/coordinationTools.ts:52-56 SERVER_SESSION_ID is a single module-level const `pid-${process.pid}-ts-${startMs}` computed ONCE per process and stamped as owner_session on EVERY claim (L117) regardless of caller. Doc comment L18 (coordinationStore.ts) + L11/L20-21 (coordinationTools.ts) state owner_session SHOULD be the per-client Claude Code session id injected by the gateway, but the live value proves the unshipped Phase-2 fallback (process pid+boot) is active. Two concurrent clients sharing one mcp-server therefore get the IDENTICAL owner_session -> a second client's claim on a held lock is treated as a re-entrant SELF-reclaim -> claimed:true -> leader-lock + per-slot mutex CANNOT serialize concurrent dispatchers.
items.raw_verification: router dev-team tick 2026-06-26T05:22Z + PO RAW-confirm via task_list_held: SIX concurrent locks across FOUR distinct owner_agents (dev-team, unified-agent, cowork-dispatcher, cowork-team) ALL carry the IDENTICAL owner_session pid-1-ts-1782423559593 (server uptime ~7.8h, matches auditor Tier-1 7h33m). Older locks from prior server lifetimes carry DIFFERENT ts (1782401745780, 1782362316958, ...) confirming owner_session rotates ONLY on mcp-server restart, NOT per client. Code root confirmed in coordinationTools.ts:52-56,117.
items.observed_impact: cowork DOUBLE-FIRE this session: news-scout-sentiment spawned twice (a89c1b41@05:02 + a404d93d@05:03); chef slots fired twice (a29c5bcd@05:16 + parallel@05:21). BOUNDED not corrupting: published:<slot>:<date|hour> marker gate prevented double MARKET posts; gatherers have E3/exec-proof idempotency. Damage = wasted spawns/fetches, not bad data.

items.title: SBV-FX (+news) SLA: post-publish-window relaxation + poll-cadence tolerance band
items.root_cause: getSlaThreshold() (freshnessSlaChecker.ts L646-652) applies the tight defaultThresholdMinutes (30) for the WHOLE VN business day whenever isVnSbvBusinessDay(now)==true. But SBV publishes FX once/day; its publish window ends 10:00 UTC (lastExpectedSbvWindowEnd L530). After 10:00Z no new sbv_fx arrives until the next business-day window, yet the 30-min tight SLA stays active all day -> age sawtooths against the ~30-min fetcher poll cadence and breaches HIGH at the top of every cycle (Fri 10:33Z age 37/30). The DONE FIX-SLA-EXEMPT-NEWS-SBVFX relaxes ONLY on non-business days (weekend/holiday); the post-publish-window-on-a-business-day window AND the SLA==poll-cadence sawtooth are uncovered. Same structural pattern hits news (tight 30-min SLA for the whole 00:00-14:59Z window vs ~30-min poll -> news sawtoothed OK->32/30 in the same tick). Same over-fire CLASS as B-11 (market-hours-blind) and C-06 (off-market).
items.fix_spec: 1) Post-window relaxation on business days: in the SBV branch, once now is PAST lastExpectedSbvWindowEnd for today, switch to (minutesSinceLastSbvWindowEnd + grace) instead of the tight 30-min -> the tight SLA applies DURING the expected publish window only, not all day. Mirror for news post-14:59Z. 2) Tolerance band so SLA never equals poll cadence: breach HIGH only when age > MAX(threshold*1.5, threshold + pollCadence); a 30-min SLA on a 30-min poller must not fire on a single-cycle slip. Apply uniformly to news + sbv_fx.
items.generic_mandate: Derive publish-window-end + poll-cadence from config per source; do NOT hardcode per-source magic. The post-window relaxation + tolerance band must cover BOTH news and sbv_fx (and be safe for any once-per-window source).
items.verification_gate: On any post-10:00Z business-day time get_sla_status returns sbv_fx ok (not HIGH); news ok post-14:59Z. A genuine >1.5x stall DURING the live publish window still breaches. Add unit tests in freshnessSlaChecker.spec for business-day-post-window + single-cycle sawtooth tolerance.
items.severity_note: Auditor B-12-POST-MARKET emitted this as WARN (not HIGH); router live get_sla_status renders it HIGH. The HIGH severity on a 6-min once-per-day-FX poll slip with market CLOSED is the over-statement this task removes.

items.root_cause: The system-auditor is contracted to ONLY append to .signal_queue.rows[], but its signal-write path (the signal-dashboard skill jq or the auditor flow orch-state write) emits a FRESH minimal-scaffold document rather than read-modify-append. It triggers ONLY on runs that emit a signal (signals_posted>=1 / signal_queue_rows_written>=1); clean 0-signal runs do not write orch-state and are harmless -- which is why dozens of clean auditor runs this session were fine and only the one signal-emitting run (de595a44) collapsed the board. Same SSOT-clobber family as jq-empty-guard-clobbers-ssot and qa-jq-nests-whole-doc-into-lane.
items.fix_spec: Architect ROOT-CAUSE the auditor signal-write path BEFORE any fix (recurring-bug-escalation). The write MUST be a STRICT targeted append to .signal_queue.rows[] with: (a) a non-empty-input guard ([ -s tmp ] + jq -e) so an empty/failed jq never replaces the file; (b) a post-write CONSERVATION check that .task_board.backlog and .task_board.{ready,in_progress,review,done,done_verified} + active_sprints counts did NOT decrease -- abort+restore from the pre-write copy if they did; (c) atomic temp->rename. NEVER emit a full-document scaffold. INTERIM MITIGATION (already applied operationally by router): until the durable fix ships, system-auditor routes findings via Telegram BUG channel + notebook ONLY and does NOT write the orch-state signal_queue -- this removes the collapse trigger entirely.
items.generic_mandate: Any agent/skill that writes orch-state.json MUST read-modify-write a targeted path, never emit a scaffold; guard with non-empty-input check + conservation check + atomic temp->rename. The conservation guard belongs in the shared signal-write helper so every emitter inherits it, not per-caller.
items.verification_gate: Add a regression test that runs the auditor signal-write against a POPULATED board fixture (>=312 backlog, >=97 signal rows) with signals_posted>=1 and asserts: backlog length preserved, signal_queue.rows length == pre+N (only appended), head not nulled, all lanes remain arrays (no array->object nesting). Test must FAIL against the current scaffold-emitting code and PASS after the fix.

items.title: Same-tick CHEF mutual-exclusion in cowork dispatch — suppress non-guaranteed chef-* slots when a guaranteed chef slot matches the same tick, in BOTH pressure modes (closes legacy-mode cadence-bypass double-publish)
items.root_cause: Two independent gaps both fire on the once-per-weekday 05:15 nominal tick where chef-morning cron (15 5) and chef-intraday cron (13 2-8) coincide: (1) pressure-state.stale_warning=true (DETERMINISTIC — cycle-snapshot age > _staleness_threshold_minutes=20, correctly reporting stale data) forces PRESSURE_MODE=legacy at Step 4.2; legacy mode sets CADENCE_MATCHES = raw MATCHES with NO filtering (pressure-cadence.md Step 4.5b), so the cadence gate that would have suppressed chef-intraday (off-market default 240min vs ~62min elapsed) is bypassed. (2) No same-tick CHEF mutex: published-marker keys differ per slot (published:chef-morning:DATE vs published:chef-intraday:DATE:HH) so they never collide, and chef-intraday's conditional logic does not detect the guaranteed morning dish that published 0-1min earlier.
items.fix_spec: Fix A (robust, per payload §06:21Z): add an UNCONDITIONAL same-tick CHEF mutual-exclusion in the dispatch tick (runs in BOTH adaptive AND legacy modes, because legacy mode is entered LEGITIMATELY whenever pressure data is stale). After MATCHES is resolved (pressure-cadence.md Step 4.5b rebind, or match-slots.md Step 4b collision guard): if MATCHES contains a guaranteed chef-* slot (slot.guaranteed==true AND slot_id matches ^chef-), drop every non-guaranteed chef-* slot from MATCHES for that tick and log a suppression telemetry line. Do NOT touch emit_pressure_state / stale_warning (fix C) — the flag is deterministic and correctly reports stale snapshots; suppressing it would mask real staleness.

Fix: change the registerTool call to server.registerTool("sequential_market_analysis", {title,description,inputSchema:tool.schema}, tool.handle) (schema+handler as SEPARATE positional args, matching the SDK contract every other tool file in this repo already uses via the server.tool(name,description,schema,handler) 4-arg legacy API — see apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/market-data/marketTools.ts:147 for the working pattern).

CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING: git show 1b1397025^:apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/analysis/sequential-market-analysis.ts shows a byte-identical broken registerTool call BEFORE the FACTORY-INTERFACE-sequential-confidence-05-mask confidence-fabrication fix landed — that fix never touches registerSequentialMarketAnalysisTools, zero relationship to this defect.

(In 'originalHandler(args)', 'originalHandler' is undefined)"}],"isError":true},...}.

items.title: Harden notebook-write AC-5 from advisory prose to BLOCKING (exit 1 -> force recompose) + commit headless-path hook backstop into repo
items.desc: ROOT CAUSE (router pass #11, raw-verified 2026-06-15): notebook-write SKILL layer-1 gate is advisory PROSE not a hard bash gate. AC-5 (SKILL line 76) is explicitly 'a verification gate, NOT a remediation loop' — it only echoes a warning, never exit 1/blocks. This CONTRADICTS the governance founding principle (project_context_bloat_governance line 13: 'Hard bash gate, not prose — haiku skips prose'). Evidence: ops.md re-breached to 237L (working-tree; HEAD 151L) AFTER its own agent-father retrofit 1c8a5ea7; the 237L write minted NO context-bloat signal (layer-2 PostToolUse hook is record-only exit 0 AND lives in gitignored .claude/settings.local.json so headless/cron/cloud spawns don't carry it). Layer-3 janitor is the ONLY hard remediation and it's reactive — board is littered with recurring CLEAN-NB-TRIM-* / FU-NB-PRUNE-* tasks (CLEAN-NB-TRIM-BATCH = 5 notebooks 297/223/223/218/228L; CLEAN-CONTEXT-BLOAT-NOTEBOOKS-20260614; CLEAN-NB-TRIM-PDFX-2; FU-NB-PRUNE-DEV-VPS), proving the reactive churn. SCOPE (the cheap correct slice — NOT a full architecture sprint): (1) Convert AC-5 to BLOCKING for the in-session/compliant-tooling path: after the settled write, if wc -l > cap then exit 1 and force the agent to recompose+re-write (a hard gate can only FAIL the write, NOT auto-pick which sections to drop — semantic prune needs agent judgment, that is the accepted tradeoff). (2) Close the headless/cron gap: commit the PostToolUse backstop hook wiring into a REPO-TRACKED settings file (.claude/settings.json, NOT .local) so cron/headless/cloud spawns carry it — OR add a documented dumb-tail-truncate fallback in the hook for non-compliant writes as a last-resort self-heal (architect decides truncate-vs-fail-vs-signal-only). DESIGN TRADEOFF to resolve in brief: dumb tail-cut loses the newest section (usually the current cycle's content) — may be unacceptable; a fail-the-write gate can't run in a fire-and-forget headless write that has no agent loop to recompose. Architect weighs blocking-in-session + signal-only-headless vs truncate-headless.

items.po_occurrence_20260729T1049Z: PO OCCURRENCE 2026-07-29T10:49Z (po, measured — NOT from the auditor self-report). The violating commit dbbd8a0fa (chore(memory/system-auditor): notebook 2026-07-29 tier-2) landed 12:35:52 +0200 = 10:35:52Z — i.e. 1h12m AFTER the last fix commit. Diff: 13 insertions / 110 deletions on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md. Exactly ONE section heading was removed (## ad265f86 · 2026-07-29T06:38:49Z) = an authorized drop-oldest; the remaining ~98 deleted lines came out of the RETAINED 07:09:23Z section, and `git show dbbd8a0fa | grep "^-"` shows TWO `### RAW-PROBE:` blocks deleted. NO CAP PRESSURE EXISTED: pre-commit 133L + 13L new = 146L against the 200L cap, so the authorized ladder (trim own section, then drop oldest) never needed to reach a retained section at all. This is therefore a clean instance of AC-3s ordering violation with the cap-pressure excuse removed, i.e. the compose step mutates retained sections even when it has no reason to. Its payload is: "[sweep-guard] BARE commit about to absorb 1 staged file(s) not necessarily this actors own: docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md ... mode=warn". That is the BARE-COMMIT peer-index sweep guard, a DIFFERENT guard detecting a DIFFERENT defect (missing pathspec). It says nothing about retained-section bytes. So "detection works, enforcement is off" is unsupported, and flipping GIT_NOTEBOOK_IMMUTABILITY_MODE=reject would NOT have caught this commit — do not treat the reject-mode transition as the remedy for this row. items.title: RECURRING DATA LOSS: the notebook-write compose step silently REWRITES the content of RETAINED prior sections to pay for an over-cap current section, instead of trimming its own section first - and the skill has no immutability invariant, so a diff reviewer cannot tell authorized pruning from unauthorized rewriting
items.premise_correction_read_first: The incoming report framed this as 'zero deletions were required, it dropped 82 lines anyway', arithmetic from the commit's NET +43/-82 diffstat. THAT PREMISE IS WRONG and an implementer who chases it will fix nothing. The new section is 71L, not 43L; 152 + 71 = 223 > 200, so cap pressure was REAL and deletions WERE required. The defect is not that it deleted - it is WHICH bytes it deleted and that no rule forbids them.
items.measured_evidence: PO measured per-section line counts on both sides of 9b27e9723 (7 sections/152L -> 6 sections/113L). BEFORE -> AFTER: 05:08:58Z 81L -> 10L REWRITTEN; d4-auto 03:00 3L -> 3L intact; x1b5c2a9 02:33 25L -> 10L REWRITTEN; d986065c 00:42 10L -> DROPPED; 88ec89d6 00:36 14L -> 10L REWRITTEN; a1f7k9x5 23:39 10L -> 9L REWRITTEN; 60d26f9b 23:10 9L -> DROPPED; new section 06:09:36Z = 71L. So FOUR retained sections had their content silently rewritten, on top of two whole-section drops. The immediately-prior cycle's own audit record was compressed 81L -> 10L.
items.defect: THREE findings. (1) LADDER ORDER INVERTED: the new section is 71L against the AC-6 cap of <=60L per section. AC-3 Step 1f prescribes an ordered remedy whose FIRST step is 'If current-cycle section > 60L: trim to 60L first'. The agent skipped its own trim and paid the cap out of other sections' content. The spec-compliant outcome was reachable: trim 71->60 (212L), drop oldest 60d26f9b (203L), drop next-oldest a1f7k9x5 (193L) -> 5 sections, ~193L, every retained section BYTE-IDENTICAL. Actual outcome: 6 sections, 113L, four retained sections mutated. (2) NO IMMUTABILITY INVARIANT: nothing in AC-1..AC-6 of .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md states that retained sections are immutable. Steps 1c and 1f authorise DROPPING whole oldest blocks; no clause authorises editing a retained block's content, and no clause forbids it. Because AC-3 lands the result as ONE whole-file Write/Edit, both authorized pruning and unauthorized rewriting appear in the commit diff as plain deletions - they are indistinguishable to any reviewer. That is why this ran for multiple cycles unnoticed. (3) SPEC SELF-CONTRADICTION: AC-2 says 'Keep: current cycle + 2 prior sections = last 3 total', but AC-3 Step 1c says drop ONE oldest per cycle. Under Step 1c the section count is INVARIANT (add one, drop one), so AC-2's steady state of 3 is unreachable from above - this notebook sat at 7 sections, which AC-2 forbids and Step 1c permits indefinitely. Whichever is normative, the other is wrong.
items.acceptance: (1) The skill states an explicit IMMUTABILITY INVARIANT: sections retained across a cycle are byte-identical before and after. The ONLY authorized mutations are dropping a whole oldest block, the AC-2b intra-prune of a named permanent accumulator, and trimming the CURRENT cycle's own section. (2) AC-2 and AC-3 Step 1c are reconciled into one rule and the doc states which is normative. (3) The cap-pressure ladder ordering is made explicit and mandatory: trim own section to <=60L FIRST, then drop oldest whole blocks, NEVER mutate a retained section to make room. (4) A MECHANICAL check - runnable by the agent or a hook - that compares retained-section bytes before and after the settled write and fails if any surviving section changed. This is the AC that makes the class detectable at all; do not drop it for being harder than the prose ACs. (5) SCOPE FENCE: do NOT fix this in scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh. That is a DIFFERENT actuator (a PostToolUse hook running AFTER the write) and already carries its own 4-row REVIEW cluster: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH, FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNER-LINE-ONLY-SETPOINT-BYTE-CAP-NEVER-CONVERGES, FIX-NOTEBOOK-LINECAP-SWEEP-BYTE-BLIND-BACKSTOP, FIX-ALERT-COMMANDER-NOTEBOOK-SINGLE-BLOB-UNPRUNABLE. This row is the agent's IN-MEMORY compose step, AC-3 Step 1, which runs BEFORE the hook ever sees the file. (6) The fix applies to the shared skill and therefore to all 37 APPEND-class agents in AC-6, not to system-auditor alone.
items.blast_radius: .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md is the shared end-of-cycle write path for the 37 agents listed in its AC-6 APPEND class. If the compose step can rewrite retained history for system-auditor it can do so for all of them, and durable audit history is the one artifact the fleet cannot reconstruct.

FIVE distinct defects, all in one file, all mechanical: (1) NUMBERING non-monotonic across the entire visible window: 84,83,85,73,5. (2) ORDERING inverted: Step 1e mandates NEWEST-FIRST insertion at TOP, yet the three newest entries by timestamp (00:14, 01:19, 01:30) sit progressively LOWER in the file — i.e. those cycles APPENDED at EOF instead of composing a settled newest-first body, which is only possible if Step 1's compose ladder was not executed as written. (3) SECTION CAP breached: 5 real sections retained against a hard cap of 3 (Step 1d 'WHILE (section count) >3: drop the LAST ## block'). (4) LINE CAP breached: 426L against the AC-5 200L cap, i.e. Step 1f's 200L backstop also did not run. (5) A stray literal '## RETURN' heading at L309 pasted INSIDE the c73 section body — a level-2 heading in the notebook body poisons every consumer that counts '^## ' headings: Step 1a PRE_COUNT, Step 2a's ACTUAL_DROPS/EXPECTED_DROPS guard, Step 1d's prune loop, scripts/notebook-auto-prune.sh, and pre-commit _check_notebook_immutability. Step 2a is the documented 'interim backstop, MANDATORY, BLOCKING' that was supposed to catch exactly this and revert via `git checkout --`; with PRE_COUNT=4/5 and ACTUAL_DROPS=0 against EXPECTED_DROPS=2/3 it should have printed [notebook-compose-guard] ABORT and reverted on at least the last two cycles. It did not. CONTENT IS CORRECT throughout (router RAW-verified every claimed report against its source) — this is purely a write-mechanism defect, no false findings were published. HYPOTHESIS REFUTED, DO NOT CHASE IT: the router's prime suspect was docs/agent-memory/.auditor-cycle-markers-*.tmp driving the counter. It does not. Per main.md L282-287 those files are per-cycle OUTPUT-CONTRACT marker scratch keyed by $FIRE_TICK and consumed only by scripts/audit-output-contract.sh; nothing in the numbering path reads them. They are, however, independent evidence of a THIRD non-executing step (see status_note).

items.title: Bound rag-service _build_fts_index() memory + wall-time so the nightly FTS rebuild completes at ANY corpus size (currently OOM-crashes the 768m container at ~56k rows)
items.note: ROOT CAUSE of ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-REBUILD-CRON qa-BLOCK (qa 2af76decc, reproduced 2/2). _build_fts_index() (apps/rag-service/infrastructure/repositories.py:325-345) calls LanceDB-native create_index('title'/'summary', config=FTS(), replace=True) over the full rag_entries table; at the corpus's current ~56254 rows (4x the DFR-P3 14k-row design premise) the build pins memory 90-99.9% of the 768m cgroup ceiling (docker-compose.yml ~L159) for 250s+ then hard-restarts the container (RestartCount 258->260). Fix MUST be corpus-size-INDEPENDENT (the corpus only grows via ongoing ragIndex() writes — the exact growth this whole cron exists to keep the BM25 leg fresh against). START by investigating whether LanceDB FTS build at the pinned version (0.33.0 Docker / 0.25.3 local) exposes a bounded-memory / on-disk writer-heap config (e.g. writer_heap_size, with_position=False, Tantivy budget); if the native builder cannot be bounded below a sane ceiling, escalate findings with concrete fallbacks (modest ops-gated mem-limit bump as belt-and-suspenders, or a chunked/segmented rebuild). NOT user-gated (rag-service code; deploys via normal gated rebuild). NO active incident — cron is deploy-pending, rag-service stable-at-rest 26% idle; this is a pre-deploy capacity fix, not an outage.

PO RAW re-check 2026-08-15T03:22-03:27Z (review-lane secondary-drain; first look since the 2026-08-12 time-gate matured). THREE new facts, all decision-relevant — this is NOT the same conclusion re-derived.

(1) GROWTH RATE HALVED, MY OWN 07-29 PROJECTION WAS WRONG BY ~3 WEEKS. Live GET :5002/embed/health index_size=30618->30619 rows (measured 03:22:35Z / 03:26Z, still climbing, re-embed pipeline ALIVE). Prior points: 116 (07-15T16:01Z), 297 (07-15T17:28Z), 10183 (07-28T19:00Z), 11243 (07-29T05:20Z). Realised rate over the 406.0h since the 07-29 note = 47.7 rows/h, NOT the 103 rows/h that note projected (that figure came off a 10.3h window and was not representative). Corpus is at 54% of the 56254-row failure scale; 25636 rows remain => ~537h => ~2026-09-06, not the ~2026-08-16 I projected. The 2026-08-12 recheck date was therefore correct to fire but the answer is still "not yet".

(2) AC#1 AND test_plan NAME A CEILING THAT NO LONGER EXISTS — AC IS FACTUALLY STALE. Both texts say "768m cgroup ceiling". Commit 2f835ec63 (2026-08-06T13:00:35Z, delivered by sibling row FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY) raised rag-service deploy.resources.limits.memory 768m->1g and reservations 256m->512m. RAW-verified live this tick: docker-compose.yml rag-service block reads "memory: 1g"; docker inspect MemLimit=1073741824. A qa agent re-running AC#1 verbatim would have measured against a ceiling that has not existed for 9 days. CORRECTED IN-PLACE THIS TICK (768m -> 1g in acceptance_criteria #1 and test_plan (b)); original 768m figure preserved in .note and in this field as historical context. This is an AC factual correction, not a scope change — the fix requirement (corpus-size-INDEPENDENT memory) is untouched.

(3) HEADROOM, NOT CORPUS SCALE, IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT — AND THE CAP RAISE DID NOT BUY ANY. Live idle baseline 858.6MiB / 1GiB = 83.85%, FLAT across 3 samples 4s apart, model_loaded=true/state=warm, ZERO FTS activity. Compare this row's own qa_result.idle_baseline_flag (07-15): ~92% of 768m ~= 707MiB. Absolute idle RSS grew ~707 -> ~859MiB (+152MiB) while the cap rose by 256MiB — i.e. the 768m->1g raise was consumed almost entirely by baseline growth and left only ~165MiB of headroom for the FTS build AC#1 wants to observe. (Caveat recorded deliberately: a 03:22:35Z sample read 864.2MiB at model_loaded=false/state=cold, which LOOKS like index-resident growth dominating, but RSS is not returned to the OS on model unload, so that reading is NOT sound evidence for attributing the baseline to the LanceDB index. Do not build a projection on it — I nearly did.)

WHY THIS STILL DOES NOT GET DISPATCHED TO QA, despite the time-gate maturing. The test is now ONE-SIDED, not simply unavailable: with ~165MiB headroom a GREEN (rebuild completes, memory trace stays flat) WOULD be genuinely informative and would substantially de-risk this row even at 54% corpus — but a RED is UNATTRIBUTABLE between "this row's fix failed" and "the unresolved idle-baseline/leak ate the headroom before the build started". That is the exact mirror image of the false-GREEN at 116 rows that caused done_verified to be withheld in the first place, and shipping a false-RED here would be the same error with the sign flipped. Second, independent reason: sibling P0 FIX-RAG-LANCECORE-OOM-PERSISTS-AFTER-THREADPIN-DEPLOYED is LIVE in qa[] on this same container and needs a >=24h dmesg-clean durability window; deliberately memory-stressing the container now would contaminate it. Cost of waiting is low (ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-REBUILD-CRON is BLOCKED but deploy-pending, no active incident); cost of a mid-window OOM is high.

BLOCKER RE-CLASSIFIED. blocked_on was "rag-corpus-repopulation-to-representative-scale" (pure wall-clock). It is now COMPOUND: corpus scale AND container headroom, the latter gated on the sibling P0 landing. Waiting on corpus alone no longer makes this testable — the FTS build's demand grows with the corpus while the idle baseline appears to grow with it too, so headroom is being squeezed from both ends. A pure "wait for 56k" hold could plausibly arrive at a container that is over its cap at idle.

GATE TO LIFT WITHHELD (unchanged in substance, sharpened): re-run AC#1 (POST /admin/rebuild-fts, docker stats peak-mem, 2x) once BOTH (a) FIX-RAG-LANCECORE-OOM-PERSISTS-AFTER-THREADPIN-DEPLOYED is DONE_VERIFIED and rag-service idle RSS leaves real headroom under the 1g cap, and (b) corpus is at/near representative scale (~2026-09-06 at current rate). If (a) clears well before (b), an early attempt IS defensible on the one-sided-test logic above — a GREEN at ~40k rows with a healthy baseline is worth more than another month of waiting; a RED at that point should NOT be read as a verdict on this row.

Seeding a throwaway rag-service container at the same 1g cap with a synthetic >=56k-row corpus would decouple this row from BOTH the live-corpus wall clock AND the live-container leak, and could close a deadlock that is now 1 month old. Naive wall-clock arithmetic over the 196.6h since then gives 7.96 rows/h vs the 47.7 rows/h recorded in po_timegate_recheck_20260815 — a 6x apparent collapse, which under this row's own escape clause ("if the growth rate collapses to ~0 before then, that IS a new defect (re-embed pipeline stalled) and needs its own row") would justify minting. IT IS AN ARTIFACT AND PO DID NOT MINT. Cause: the whole host/Docker scheduler was silent 2026-08-18T09:00Z -> 2026-08-22T12:40Z (~99.7h), with a degraded shoulder 08-15..08-18 running at 0.5-5% of baseline. Proof read directly from cron_job_runs in /app/data/market.db: daily run counts 08-13=3146, 08-14=3147, 08-15=1584, 08-16=18, 08-17=42, 08-18=154, 08-19/20/21=NO ROWS, 08-22=1215, 08-23=889; intelligenceCycle (15m cadence) fired last on 08-18 09:xx then nothing until 08-22 12:40 then exactly 4/hour since. Subtracting dead+degraded time leaves roughly 25-30 live hours in that window, so the ingest rate per LIVE hour is ~52-63 rows/h, i.e. equal to or better than the 47.7 baseline. The re-embed pipeline is HEALTHY. Do not open a stalled-ingest row on this evidence.

(2) THE AC CEILING IS STALE FOR THE SECOND TIME — 768m -> 1g -> 2g.
AC#1 and test_plan still say "768m cgroup ceiling". po_timegate_recheck_20260815 already corrected that to 1g (commit 2f835ec63). It is now WRONG AGAIN: live `docker inspect` on vn-market-intelligence-mcp-rag-service-1 reports MemLimit=2147483648 = 2 GiB. A qa agent re-running AC#1 verbatim would measure against a ceiling that has not existed for two revisions. THE AC TEXT MUST BE CORRECTED BEFORE ANY RE-RUN.

(3) THE ROW'S FAILURE PREMISE MAY NO LONGER HOLD AT ALL.
Original premise: the FTS build "pins memory 90-99.9% of the 768m cgroup ceiling for 250s+ then hard-restarts the container". Live now: rag-service is Up 7 days, RestartCount=0, OOMKilled=false, StartedAt 2026-08-15T10:16:22Z, using 779.2MiB of 2GiB = 38.05%, i.e. ~1.27GiB of headroom where the original failure had ~0. The absolute peak that killed a 768m container would not necessarily kill a 2GiB one. That does NOT mean the row is fixed — the row's actual requirement is that the build be corpus-size-INDEPENDENT, and a bigger ceiling only buys headroom, it does not bound the slope.

(4) PO DECISION — SPLIT THE ACs. AC#2 IS TESTABLE TODAY; AC#1 STAYS TIME-GATED.
AC#2 ("report the completed rebuild's steady-state PEAK MEMORY + WALL-CLOCK time — this number sizes ALPHA-S2's deadline retune AND any ops mem-limit decision") does not depend on reaching representative scale. It is measurable right now at 32184 rows and its output is the single number three other decisions are waiting on. AC#1 ("no OOM at ~56k rows") remains genuinely untestable until the corpus gets there and STAYS time-gated. Dispatch AC#2 alone.
HARD GUARD, NON-NEGOTIABLE: a green on AC#2 is NOT a green on AC#1 and MUST NOT be recorded as one. This exact row already produced that false green once — qa certified it at 116 rows in 2026-07-15 where the FTS-build memory delta over idle was ~4-5MiB, i.e. the test could not have failed. Whoever runs AC#2 must report peak-mem + wall-clock + the row count it was measured at, and explicitly leave AC#1 open.

(5) TIME-GATE RECOMPUTED HONESTLY. 56254 - 32184 = 24070 rows remaining. At the corrected ~47.7-63 rows/h of LIVE time that is ~380-500 live-hours = 16-21 days of CONTINUOUS uptime. Realised availability over the last 9 days was roughly 55%, and the previous two projections both erred optimistic (2026-08-16 became 2026-09-06). po_timegate_next_recheck_after moved 2026-09-06 -> 2026-09-20. Do not hand-re-measure the corpus before that date; the AC#2 dispatch in (4) is the work available in the meantime.

(6) NOT MERGED WITH THE OTHER TWO RAG ROWS — they are the same SUBSYSTEM, not the same FIX. OPS-RAG-SERVICE-REBUILD-DEPLOY-LANCEDB-FIX = a deploy action, verified already done and CANCELLED by PO this tick as self-declared superseded by FIX-RAG-LANCECORE-OOM-PERSISTS-AFTER-THREADPIN-DEPLOYED (qa[]). FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY = the cgroup sizing decision, deploy half verified done, durability half still owed to qa. THIS row = a code-level bound on _build_fts_index(). Merging them would hide the one that is actually still unbuilt.

(7) BLOCKED_ON LEG (a) LOOKS SATISFIED BUT PO DID NOT CLOSE IT. blocked_on names "rag-service-idle-headroom-gated-on-FIX-RAG-LANCECORE-OOM-PERSISTS-AFTER-THREADPIN-DEPLOYED (P0, qa[])". That row has not moved since 2026-08-15T10:07:25Z while the service it tracks has now held 7 days at RestartCount=0 / OOMKilled=false / 38% of a 2GiB cap. That is candidate evidence the OOM loop is over, but certifying it is qa's call and not PO's, and the standing lesson feedback_ac3_durability_certified_on_window_that_ended_before_metric_settled applies. Flagged for qa, deliberately not closed here.

items.detail: PO report-triage 2026-07-16T21:00Z. RAW-verified readonly on live named-volume market.db (docker exec vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1 bun): (1) all 12 Q4-2025 flood tickers (DBC/DXG/FRT/GEX/KDC/KDH/MSN/PDR/SAB/VIX/VJC/VND) exist in financial_reports as Q4-2025 with text_status=COMPLETE + pdf_path SET but LAYOUT=0 / TABLE_ROWS=0 / refine_status=PENDING and NO bctc_vps_queue row remaining (enrich_failed Q4-2025 queue count now 0). text_status=COMPLETE+pdf_path SET => discovery/fetch/OCR-text layers ALL healthy; the failure is purely at PEK-layout + agentic-refine structured extraction. This DEFINITIVELY rules out source-outage/VPS-down/DNS. (2) GLOBAL freshness: MAX(bctc_layout_units.extracted_at)=2026-06-10, MAX(bctc_table_rows.extracted_at)=2026-06-30 => nothing extracted for ~5wk/~2.5wk. These maxes are OLDER than SPIKE-BCTC-TABLEROWS-FROZEN-HOLLOW-DONE's 07-12 readings (that spike RAW-read layout_units growing to 07-12/1829 rows + table_rows 07-08/4091) => a DATA-LOSS/ROLLBACK event between 07-12 and 07-16 is strongly implied (cf. memory: VM-rebuild DESTROYS named volumes->restore; gateway/volume swaps). (3) bctcExtractReconcileJob walked the whole watchlist backlog backwards Q4->Q3->Q2->Q1-2025 overnight (07-15 20:05Z->07-16 07:15Z, ~1 ticker/30min) marking each enrich_failed (cap-8) and emitting ONE fail-loud telegram report per ticker*quarter = 76-report storm (PO archived all 121 overnight reports 3358-3478 as duplicate this tick to stop the re-surface churn; ACK path via process_telegram_report/markProcessed CONFIRMED working). DO-NOT-RE-TREAD (cross-ref, do not re-investigate): FIX-BCTC-PDFPULL-WIRE-TABLE-EXTRACTION (DONE_VERIFIED 07-10 — the wiring; THIS spike asks why it is not PRODUCING in current prod, not to re-design it); SPIKE-BCTC-TABLEROWS-FROZEN-HOLLOW-DONE (hollow-done + refine-cron dormancy F4/F5); FIX-BCTC-REFINE-DURABLE-TRIGGER-BACKSTOP (table_rows producer durable backstop — the refine half); FIX-BCTC-D3C-FOLLOW-UP-RESET-ATTEMPTS (Arm-2 7d recycle re-exhausts because reconcile_attempts not zeroed — the per-row recycle mechanism); SPIKE-BCTC-REPARSE-CADENCE-GUARD-ROOTCAUSE-VERIFY (cadence guard). NET-NEW value = (a) infra rollback verification, (b) why extraction dormant since mid-June despite DONE_VERIFIED fix (cron registered+firing? PEK producing? fix effect reverted by rollback?), (c) a report-storm circuit-breaker so bctcExtractReconcileJob cannot emit one fail-loud per ticker*quarter against a systemically-dormant producer. || [po-triage-20260805T0908Z] PREMISE REFUTED — RE-SCOPE BEFORE ANY WORK. This row title and question both assert the structured-extraction pipeline is DORMANT (bctc_layout_units frozen 2026-06-10, bctc_table_rows frozen 2026-06-30) and hypothesise a DB-restore/VM-rebuild rollback. That was accurate on 2026-07-16. It is FALSE on 2026-08-05. RAW readonly probe of the live named-volume DB this tick: bctc_layout_units n=5134, MAX(extracted_at)=2026-08-04 22:12:12, per-day writes 07-28:159 / 08-01:1430 / 08-02:430 / 08-03:1865 / 08-04:463. bctc_vps_queue status=done n=171 spanning 2023-Q4 through 2026-Q2 (incl. 7 done in 2023-Q4 and 11 in 2024-Q4 — historical backfill IS succeeding). The layout-extraction stage is alive and productive. Nobody should spend a timebox looking for a rollback event that the data says did not persist. Dropping P0 -> P1 accordingly: the original emergency is over. || THE 2026-08-03/04 REPORT STORM IS A DIFFERENT BUG, ALREADY ROOT-CAUSED. 45 RECONCILE-EXHAUSTED/CIRCUIT-BREAKER reports fired 08-03T06:05Z-08-04T18:05Z. Cause is NOT dormancy: 66 financial_reports rows carry fallback-<TICKER>-<YEAR>-<Q> ids (all 66 with data_env=production, vs 191 UUID rows all with data_env=NULL — a perfect 1:1 partition), and 0 of those 66 has ever produced a layout_unit or table_row, so the reconcile predicate reads 0 by construction and terminalises + fires a fail-loud BUG every pass. Minted as FIX-BCTC-FALLBACK-SHELL-REPORTS-STRUCTURALLY-UNEXTRACTABLE (P0, architect). That row supersedes the report-storm half of this SPIKE. || WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN AND UNTRACKED — THE REAL QUESTION FOR THIS ROW: a STAGE DIVERGENCE inside the live pipeline. bctc_layout_units MAX(extracted_at)=2026-08-04 22:12:12 but bctc_table_rows MAX(extracted_at)=2026-08-01 16:39:07. The layout stage has written on 08-02, 08-03 and 08-04; the table-row stage has written NOTHING for ~4 days. Per-day table_rows: 07-29:451, 07-30:391, 07-31:109, 08-01:652, then zero. Two consecutive stages of one pipeline, one alive and one silent — the layout->table_rows handoff is the suspect. This is NOT covered by the fallback row (that cohort never reaches either stage) and is NOT covered by FIX-BCTC-PDFPULL-WIRE-TABLE-EXTRACTION (closed 07-10, and demonstrably working since). RE-SCOPE THIS SPIKE TO: why did bctc_table_rows stop accepting writes on 2026-08-01T16:39Z while bctc_layout_units kept producing? || The emission circuit-breaker this SPIKE asked for was HALF-SHIPPED and is working as far as it goes: reports 4313/4356/4363/4373 are RECONCILE CIRCUIT BREAKER TRIPPED run-summaries with per-row BUGs suppressed. It only trips at >=3 exhausted rows in one run, so single-row runs still emit one BUG each — 41 of the 45 reports came through that gap. Lowering the trip threshold (or suppressing by known-unresolvable class) belongs with the fallback row fix.

items.title: pdf-extractor's uvicorn PARENT process (PID 1) -- not tesseract concurrency, which is already fixed and proven bounded -- is the dominant memory driver, and the row's OOM-risk business case remains open: VmHWM=2,541,184kB (~2.42 GiB, ~97% of the 2.5 GiB cap) was recorded inside this container's post-fix life, which would leave the just-shipped AC-4 bar (<=80% of cap) violated at peak even though it is satisfied at trough
items.root_cause: MECHANISM (qa+router corroborated, both read-only): a load-correlated SAWTOOTH in the parent uvicorn process, released at job boundaries -- NOT accumulation/climbing; that framing was explicitly refuted by direct observation and must not be carried forward. (1) VmHWM (all-time high-water mark since container start 2026-07-28T16:45:08Z, RestartCount=0) = 2,541,184 kB -- a real peak reached ~97% of the 2.5 GiB cap at least once in this container's post-fix life, proving the ceiling is reachable. (2) qa's own re-sample ~23min after the concurrency-fix rebuild, under ordinary (non-burst) traffic: MemPerc 78-83%, PID1 (uvicorn) alone RSS ~2.0-2.1 GiB (~83-84% of the container BY ITSELF) while tesseract stayed bounded at 0-1 (~90-95 MiB each) -- the now-fixed tesseract concurrency is not the term driving the container back toward the cap. (3) auditor samples 45.18% (17:10:56Z) and 44.74% (17:16:32Z) -- stable/declining in that window, consistent with a trough. (4) router's own 10-sample series 17:18:46Z-17:21:47Z: PID1 RSS held 1.08-1.11 GiB with tesseract=1 in-flight; at 17:21:06Z tesseract dropped to 0 and MemPerc fell to 40.44%; at 17:21:26Z tesseract returned to 1 and RSS jumped 1.24->1.39 GiB in one sample -- RSS moving WITH an OCR job starting/stopping, not monotonically, by a magnitude (100s of MiB per job) that dwarfs a single tesseract child's own footprint. (5) parent dominance: PID1 RSS ~2.0-2.1 GiB at peak vs tesseract child ~90-95 MiB -- the child term was already proven bounded by FIX-PDFX-TESSERACT-CONCURRENCY-VIOLATES-SINGLE-WORKER-INVARIANT; this row is specifically the PARENT term, a different mechanism in a different process from that row's fix.  ||  EVIDENCE ADDENDUM 2026-08-01T06:08Z-06:17Z (po/triage-auditor-findings-20260801, read-only: docker inspect + docker stats + docker exec cat /proc/1/status + /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.* + docker logs). THIS ADDENDUM FALSIFIES THIS ROW OWN PRIOR root_cause ON ONE POINT -- read it before planning. (1) THE BURST IS NOT RELEASED AT THE JOB BOUNDARY. A 47-page PekEngineAdapter job ran to successful completion at 06:09:53.913Z ("_run_pek_extract: DONE report_id=486980a8-2b61-4e02-8bf1-65166542670c push_echo_units=47 push_echo_pages=47"). From 06:10:01Z to 06:16:59Z -- 40 consecutive samples at 8-15s spacing, entirely AFTER that completion, with tesseract child count 0 in every sample -- PID1 (uvicorn/python3) VmRSS was BYTE-IDENTICAL at 2521008 kB in all 40 samples, VmHWM constant at 2641368 kB, and cgroup memory.current oscillated only 2609258496-2610274304 B (+/-0.04%). At 06:17Z ps inside the container showed PID1 python3 RSS 2521008 kB as the ONLY non-transient process. 2521008 kB = 2.404 GiB = 96.2% of the 2.5 GiB cap HELD AT IDLE, with zero work in flight. The prior root_cause clause "a load-correlated SAWTOOTH ... released at job boundaries -- NOT accumulation/climbing" does NOT hold for this container life: the down-stroke of the sawtooth did not occur. (2) RESTING STATE IS AT THE WALL. 06:08:34Z docker stats: 2.468GiB / 2.5GiB = 98.70%, PIDs=29. cgroup v2 at the same moment: memory.current=2675834880 of memory.max=2684354560 = 99.68%, memory.peak=2684391424 (i.e. peak has touched/exceeded the limit), anon=2564096000, file=52416512, slab=17084624. Container: RestartCount=2, StartedAt=2026-08-01T02:46:16.989733302Z, State.ExitCode=0, OOMKilled=false, RestartPolicy=unless-stopped, HostConfig.Memory=2684354560. Free headroom at 06:08Z was ~8.5 MB of cgroup budget -- not enough for one more page raster, let alone one more job. (3) THE FAILURE MODE IS A CLEAN EXIT, NOT AN OOM KILL. ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false with RestartPolicy=unless-stopped means this service silently self-terminates and is restarted by Docker rather than being OOM-killed, so NOTHING in the OOM-detection plane (A-30 state.oom_killed, dmesg OOM-killer) will ever witness it. Any acceptance criterion that keys on OOMKilled will pass while the service is dying. (4) LOAD CONTROL FOR THE TRAJECTORY -- CORRECTS THE BRIEF THAT PROMPTED THIS ADDENDUM. The auditor brief reported the 53%->80-82% climb as occurring at "0 extracts/30m" (i.e. an idle leak). docker logs --since 2026-08-01T02:46:00Z contradicts that: 52 POST /extract in this container life, 51 of them inside 03:27:22-03:35:38Z and 1 in hour 05. The climb window was NOT idle -- it contained a 51-job burst. So the correct reading is neither "idle leak" nor "released sawtooth": memory is acquired during jobs and RETAINED ACROSS job boundaries, producing a monotonically rising FLOOR (53% at 03:06Z -> 96.2% floor at 06:17Z after ~52 jobs). (5) QUEUE PRESSURE IS REAL: bctc_vps_queue live at 06:17Z = deferred_infra 328, enrich_failed 128, done 98, url_not_found 42, pending 13, pek_triggered 5 -- there is queued work that will re-enter this service. PRECISION CORRECTION 2026-08-01T06:23Z (same triage, extended sampler completed after the addendum was first written): the post-completion retention series is larger than stated above -- 54 consecutive samples spanning 06:10:01Z to 06:22:26Z (12min25s, two independent sampler runs, 8-15s spacing), tesseract child count 0 in every sample, PID1 VmRSS BYTE-IDENTICAL at 2521008 kB in all 54 and VmHWM constant at 2641368 kB in all 54. docker stats at 06:23:08Z: 2.406GiB / 2.5GiB = 96.25%, RestartCount still 2, StartedAt unchanged 2026-08-01T02:46:16Z. Read the "40 samples / 06:10:01Z-06:16:59Z" figure above as a subset of this series, not a second observation. LATE PARTIAL RELEASE, RECORDED FOR HONESTY AND BECAUSE IT IS DIAGNOSTIC (2026-08-01T06:25:29Z, same triage): PID1 VmRSS finally moved off the 2521008 kB plateau to 2407444 kB -- a release of 113564 kB (~111 MiB) occurring somewhere between 06:22:26Z and 06:25:29Z, i.e. roughly 12-15 MINUTES AFTER the 06:09:53Z job completion, with ZERO POST /extract in the whole 06:10Z-06:25Z interval (docker logs --since 2026-08-01T06:10:00Z | grep -c "POST /extract" = 0). VmHWM unchanged at 2641368 kB. docker stats 06:25:29Z = 92.95%. So the correct statement is NOT "memory is never released" -- it is that release is LATE, PARTIAL and DECOUPLED FROM THE JOB BOUNDARY: ~111 MiB of ~1.5 GiB acquired since the 03:06Z 53% baseline came back, out-of-band, a quarter-hour after the work finished, leaving a 2407444 kB = 91.9%-of-cap resting floor. This is the signature of deferred/opportunistic reclamation (glibc malloc arena trim, or a GC generation collected on a timer) rather than of scope-exit deallocation at the request boundary, and it is why a snapshot taken at any single moment can read as either "sawtooth" or "plateau" depending on where in this slow cycle it lands. It reinforces AC5: the three candidate mechanisms must be discriminated with an artifact, and AC6: the idle floor must be measured at least 5 minutes -- preferably 20 -- after the last job, not at the boundary.
items.deliverable: Diagnose what in the uvicorn PARENT process holds 100s of MiB-to-~1GiB per job and releases it at job boundaries (candidates, not a prescription: PDF page rasterization/image buffers held in the request-handling coroutine before/after handing a page to OCR, pdfplumber/PyMuPDF page-object retention across a multi-page document, response-body buffering, GC-deferred large objects between requests) -- name the mechanism with a captured artifact, not prose. Then size a bound so peak MemPerc stays <=80% under the SAME caller shape used to verify the concurrency fix (a 15-wide POST /extract burst), OR make an explicit, evidenced recommendation that the cap itself needs revisiting (user/ops-gated infra decision -- do not decide the cap here).
acceptance: AC1: mechanism named with a captured artifact (not prose) explaining which parent-process code path drives RSS by 100s of MiB to ~1 GiB+ per OCR job and releases it at job end.

AC2: peak docker stats MemPerc for pdf-extractor during and shortly after a 15-wide POST /extract burst (the same trigger shape already used to verify the concurrency fix) is measured and reported with raw output + date -u timestamps -- whatever the number is, report it honestly.

AC3: EITHER a change lands that keeps peak MemPerc <=80% of the 2.5 GiB cap under that burst, OR an explicit evidence-backed recommendation is written that 80%-of-cap is not achievable at the current cap for the largest real observed document, routed to ops/user for a capacity decision.
AC4: regression floor -- BCTC extraction still succeeds end-to-end on at least one real scanned PDF after any change.

AC5 (added 2026-08-01): explicitly discriminate unreleased-Python-heap vs malloc-arena-fragmentation vs deliberate-cache as the cause of the retained idle floor, with an artifact (e.g. tracemalloc/gc totals vs RSS, or a malloc_trim/jemalloc A-B) -- a fix aimed at the wrong one of these three will not move RSS.

AC6 (added 2026-08-01): the accepted bound must hold at IDLE, not only at peak -- measure PID1 VmRSS at least 5 minutes after the last job completes with tesseract child count 0, and report it. The 2026-08-01 idle floor was 2521008 kB = 96.2% of cap.

AC7 (added 2026-08-01): do NOT use OOMKilled as a success signal -- the observed failure mode is State.ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false under RestartPolicy=unless-stopped. Any regression gate must key on MemPerc/VmRSS or on RestartCount growth, never on the OOM flag.

ARCHITECT 2026-08-07T23:53Z — full blueprint: docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-07-fix-pdfx-parent-process-memory-burst-headroom.md.

AC1/AC5 MECHANISM NAMED WITH ARTIFACT: PEK pipeline (POST /pek-extract -> interface/pek_run_helper.py:_run_pek_extract -> asyncio.to_thread(pek_adapter.extract_layout_and_tables) -> PekEngineAdapter's own ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)) runs doclayout_yolo/YOLOv10 (torch CPU) + PaddleOCR PP-StructureV2 (PaddlePaddle CPU) INFERENCE DIRECTLY INSIDE PID1 — isolated only by a Python thread, unlike the already-fixed tesseract path which runs in a real ProcessPoolExecutor OS process (main.py:154, ExtractTablesUseCase only). Isolated repro (own cgroup, docker run --rm from the SAME image + model-cache volume + a real 59-page BCTC PDF, script now at scripts/audits/pdfx-pek-mem-arena-probe.py): model load alone = +845.4 MiB RSS (main.py's own "~80MB" comment is stale by >10x, flagged for correction); one layout-detection pass over the doc = +485.2 MiB (cold) / +236.4 MiB (2nd pass, steady-state); gc.collect() recovers 0 bytes both times (rules out unreleased-Python-heap as the dominant driver); malloc_trim(0) recovers 165.9 MiB / 235.6 MiB (~99.7% of the steady-state per-job delta) — CONFIRMS glibc malloc-arena-fragmentation as the dominant mechanism for the monotonic per-job floor-rise the 2026-08-01 addendum measured (53%->96.2% over 52 jobs), not deliberate-cache (which malloc_trim could not have touched) nor Python-heap retention.

AC2 GAP FOUND: the row's own literal burst spec ("15-wide POST /extract", mirroring the tesseract-fix verification) targets the WRONG endpoint — POST /extract only reaches the already-fixed, process-isolated tesseract path, never PekEngineAdapter. Corrected spec (POST /pek-extract, sequential not concurrent given the semaphore) written in the brief §5, handed to dev-pdf-extractor for ops-supervised live execution — NOT run against production by this architect cycle: the live container has already touched 98.5% of its 2.5 GiB cap in its CURRENT life (RestartCount 2->7 since the 2026-08-01 addendum, same clean-exit signature every time), so adding a memory-hungry test action to that SAME cgroup is an infrastructure/operational risk outside this role's charter (init.md not_my_job: Infrastructure diagnosis), not a diagnosis action.

AC6 idle-floor RE-MEASURED this cycle, current container life (StartedAt 2026-08-04, different life than the 2026-08-01 addendum): 1,847,472 kB (73.9% of cap) at 23:23:52Z -> 1,559,376 kB (62.4%) at 23:51:57Z, DECLINING not flat (tesseract child count 0 confirmed both times, idle >=30min confirmed via docker logs) — a second, independent data point for the row's own "late/deferred partial release" finding, this life just mid-cycle rather than at the 96.2% extreme. VmHWM=2,582,784 kB (98.5% of cap) confirms the ceiling was touched in this life too. New finding not in the row's own text: host/container swap IS active (~776 MiB of this process swapped out at the first sample) — any capacity-cap conversation should use RSS+Swap, not cgroup memory.current/docker-stats MemPerc alone, or it under-counts.

Evidence says this should recover the large majority of per-job growth and stabilize the trimmed floor (1,192,616 -> 1,193,336 kB across 2 repeated jobs in the repro, +0.06%).
