items.po_ruling_q1_20260808T113305: BLOCKER Q1 ANSWERED (publish-block policy on persistent 2nd-pass AF-4 FAIL). BA recommended reusing CHEF's existing claim-truth-gate no-override contract. PARTIALLY REJECTED — adopting it wholesale is a category error that would make this row's own AC-3 unsatisfiable by construction. AF-3's second-pass-FAIL contract (chef-dish.md:335-336) is 'write an honest gap and proceed to send (no hard block for CHEF because the message must publish)'. That is correct FOR AF-3, whose offending content may be the substance of the analysis and whose failure mode is an unfixable upstream tool gap. It is WRONG for AF-4: AF-4's offending content is a single numeric literal checked against a STATIC repo constant (25,500), so there is no 'tool could not return it' failure mode and the remedy is always available and always cheap. Letting AF-4 publish a known-wrong threshold under an honest-gap note is precisely the user-facing defect AC-3 exists to eliminate ('the 25,000 drift variant no longer publishes to MARKET') — a textbook gameable success signal. RULING — SENTENCE-SCOPED STRIP, NOT DISH-SCOPED BLOCK: on persistent 2nd-pass AF-4 FAIL, CHEF MUST (a) remove the offending numeric threshold citation from the composed text and restate it in the qualitative direction-only form the FX contract already mandates, (b) emit the honest-gap token, (c) proceed to publish. Never publish the un-reconciled numeral; never suppress the dish. i.e. adopt AF-3's publish-must-proceed half, reject its leave-the-offending-text-in-place half; the discriminant is that AF-4's offending span is always safely deletable. Exit-code 2 (SSOT constant unreadable/misconfigured) keeps AF-3's exact fail-loud path: send_telegram(channel='bug') and EXIT. Scope stays broadened to all narrative macro-threshold citations (USD/VND, gold, oil) per this row's own status_note — the strip rule is metric-agnostic. next_agent=architect may proceed on gate placement.

(1) SEQUENCING — CONFIRMED, and MORE SEVERE than described. Blueprint Design 1 AF-4 invokes .claude/skills/macro-threshold-gate/SKILL.md and its exit-2 path is send_telegram(bug)+EXIT, sited at Step 6.7 which PRECEDES Step 7's send_telegram. (2) DEAD-CODE CORRECTION — ACCEPTED, and stronger than architect stated. currencySignal/oilSignal/goldSignal/policySignal are declared `function` with NO `export` in macroTools.ts, so callers could only exist in-file; grep returns exactly one line each (its own definition). The policyTools.ts:110/116/120 hits are `policySignals`, a DIFFERENT identifier (array of PolicySignal), not calls. Provably dead. My po_goahead_20260808T113305 sub-claim "whose text ships into MARKET narrative" was WRONG — hereby RETRACTED. Replacement provenance independently re-verified, not taken on architect's word: cascadeEngine.ts:140 imports ./cascade/macroAdjustments.js, which carries 8 usdVndMarket>25500 rules.
(3) OIL ADJACENT FINDING — PREMISE FALSIFIED, DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED. Architect claims macroTools.ts(dead, >90/<70) vs macroAdjustments.ts(live, >100) is a USD/VND-shaped reconciliation gap. Raw read of the LIVE file shows it contains ALL THREE: >90 at L46-61, <70 at L65-74, >100 at L151-172/209 — with its own comments "// Brent crude > 90" and "// Brent crude > 100 -> severe oil crisis". These are deliberate SEVERITY TIERS inside one live file, and the dead code's >90/<70 MATCHES the live >90/<70 tier exactly. No contradiction therefore no reconciliation gap. Minting on this premise would create a false-premise task. Recorded here so it is not re-minted.
(4) BLOCKING — THE SSOT IS NOT SETTLED; THE ENTIRE EVIDENCE CHAIN WAS TS-ONLY. Every grep in this chain (BA §1a, my own po_goahead, architect's "independent verification" #2) used --include='*.ts'. The Go plane was NEVER searched. Raw: apps/macro-indicators/pkg/primitive/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier.go:34 `BearishThreshold = 25000.0` — a named PRODUCTION constant, compared at :85, and INTERPOLATED INTO NARRATIVE TEXT at :91: "USDVND at %.0f exceeds %.0f threshold — VND depreciation creates import cost pressure (BEARISH)", i.e. it literally emits the string "exceeds 25000 threshold". Live-wired, not dead: macro_signals.go:25 imports it and :144 calls uvnd.Classify(); usecases.go:46/194/295 wire it into the production usecase. So "25,500 is the only candidate with real production-code backing anywhere in the repo" is FALSE — an artifact of a TS-scoped grep (feedback_internal_consistency_is_not_corroboration_check_the_other_plane).
ROOT-CAUSE INVERSION: this row's founding note blames "LLM NARRATIVE DRIFT toward a historically-familiar round number (25,000 = VND's 2023 'vuot moc 25,000' media milestone), NOT a text-instruction defect". That diagnosis is now falsified. 25,000 is the literal output of the LIVE Go macro-indicators classifier feeding CHEF (architect's own note confirms registerMacroTools() calls the Go microservice on :5004). CHEF citing "25,000" was most likely FAITHFULLY RELAYING its upstream tool, not free-associating. The gate as designed would strip the very numeral CHEF's own data source produced and enforce 25500 against it — inverting this task's purpose and shipping a user-facing false-positive on genuinely tool-sourced content.
(5) BLOCKING — gold_usd:4300 has ZERO code provenance and its only source doc is ALREADY an open defect row. grep 4300 across *.ts and *.go finds no threshold constant (only unrelated fixtures: 43000000000000 equity, 24300 usd_vnd_buy, 74300 OHLCV highs). The registry's own source field admits it: "chef-dish.md Step 6, AUTO-CURE c98" — a doc, not code. Prior-art check (feedback_file_prior_art_check_before_minting_row) surfaced backlog row FIX-CHEF-L6-GOLD-FALSE-PREDICATE (priority high) ruling on that exact block: "'4300' appears in NO file except chef.md", "The tool's own gold threshold is $2200", "the cure shipped a false-claim generator", AC = "source or delete the $4,300 constant". Enshrining 4300 as canonical SSOT reintroduces the EXACT 26,500 defect shape (doc-only value, zero code backing) inside this task's own fix, and Design 4 test cases (c)/(d) bake the wrong polarity into the harness. Live cascade gold tiers are >2000/>3000/>4000.
(6) DESIGN — single-value-per-metric registry vs multi-tier live code = FALSE-POSITIVE STRIPS OF CORRECT CONTENT. The live cascade is tiered for every metric: usd_vnd >25500 (8 rules) AND <24500 (L141,L147); gold >2000/>3000/>4000; oil <70/>90/>100. Registry Design 3 gives each metric ONE scalar value+comparator. A dish correctly citing the live 24,500 lower band fails the SSOT-citation sub-check (24500 != 25500) and, under po_ruling_q1's deliberately unconditional strip, is silently destroyed. The registry needs per-metric tier SETS, not a scalar. (Note: architect's own item-3 error — reading a tiered ladder as a contradiction — is the same mistake this schema makes.)
DISPOSITION: status REVIEW->BLOCKED. NOT dispatching developer or agent-father. Building the script/skill/test now would bake 25500/4300 into the test harness and force a rebuild once the SSOT rules. What SURVIVES intact: the gate MECHANISM (alias location, bounded-window parse, comparator arithmetic, historical-context guard, per-metric number_format), the AF-4/Step-7.6 placement, the exit-code contract, and po_ruling_q1's sentence-scoped-strip. What is blocked: the registry VALUES and its schema arity.
UNBLOCK PATH: (a) FIX-USDVND-THRESHOLD-SSOT promoted BACKLOG->READY/next_agent=architect — it owns "pick one SSOT" across all three planes; NOTE the semantic question must be answered BEFORE any value is picked: Go's 25000 is a DIRECTION-band threshold (BEARISH/NEUTRAL/BULLISH, band 23000-25000) while TS's 25500 is a CASCADE-IMPACT trigger — these may be two legitimately different concepts, not one drifted constant, and collapsing them blindly would repeat the exact tier-vs-contradiction error caught in (3). (b) gold must settle via FIX-CHEF-L6-GOLD-FALSE-PREDICATE before gold enters the registry. When both land, this row resumes at architect for registry re-spec (tier sets + code-anchored provenance only), after which the developer-before-agent-father sequencing in (1) applies unchanged.

DESIGN ASK (architect, plan_only -- do NOT hand-edit spawn-fanout.md on this pass):
(A) Replace/augment Step 5.3's single known-bad string list with a TWO-ARM gate. Arm 1 (cheap, keep): positive-match markers, extended with the shapes observed here (future-tense 'Next actions (for the LLM ...)', 'would require', a STATUS token not in the slot agent's own RETURN enum). Arm 2 (LOAD-BEARING, new): a mechanical ARTIFACT-DELTA check -- for each slot, assert the declared durable artifact actually changed since spawn (git diff on a notebook/doc path, file mtime, a DB/tool row-count probe, or a new .signal_queue row) BEFORE last_fired is stamped. Arm 2 does not read the spawn's returned text at all, so no future narration shape can evade it. Precedent for the exact predicate already exists in-repo and should be reused, not reinvented: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:161-168 AC-3 states the generic rule verbatim ('any step that writes an artifact AND asserts its own persistence must re-read the persistence layer before claiming it, never trust the write call's own exit code') and scripts/audit-output-contract.sh already does marker-parsed counting for the auditor. The novelty here is applying it at the SPAWNER boundary rather than the writer's own boundary -- which is the whole point, since the writer is the unreliable party.
(B) Decide WHERE the per-slot artifact declaration lives (candidate: a new required field on each docs/data/cowork-schedule.json slot, e.g. delivery_proof: {kind: file_delta|db_probe|signal_row, target: <path|tool>}), and how a slot with no honest proof artifact is handled (explicit opt-in allowlist ONLY -- see feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist; never a silent opt-out default).
(C) SEQUENCING -- MANDATORY, do not skip: reconcile with TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-6 (FR-7, 'Rewrite last-fired.md Step 5b as reconciliation logic', BACKLOG, next=developer) and with the standing PO ruling on FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY (po_consolidation_ruling_20260728: do not route the subsumed rows until the BA-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP epic closes). CATCHUP-6 makes last_fired a RECONCILED value (backfilled from task_list_held claimed_at); this row makes last_fired a GATED value (refused without delivery proof). Those are complementary but must not become two competing authorities over the same field -- the brief must state which one owns the write and how they compose. If architect judges this belongs INSIDE the CATCHUP epic as an added FR rather than as a standalone row, say so explicitly and route it there; that is an acceptable and expected outcome of this design pass.
(D) CRON-SPAWNED COVERAGE (the occurrence-2 half): cron-fired agents (system-auditor tiers, and any other non-cowork spawn) have NO exogenous observer at all. Note the already-designed mitigation in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-06-fix-system-auditor-cycle-notebook-persistence-lifecycle.md (3a stale-marker sweep) DOES NOT cover occurrence 2: RAW-verified there is no docs/agent-memory/.auditor-cycle-markers-2026-08-06T*.tmp on disk at all (the 6 orphans present are 07-30T16:00Z, 07-31T00:00Z, 08-01T04:00Z, 08-05T17:30Z, 08-05T18:00Z, 08-05T19:00Z) -- the 09:52Z spawn died BEFORE Step 0d ever created $MARKERS_FILE, so a sweep keyed on orphaned markers is blind to it. Whatever exogenous observer is proposed for cron-spawned agents must trigger on the ABSENCE of an expected cycle artifact for a due tick, not on the presence of an orphaned one. This sub-finding must also be relayed onto FIX-SYSTEM-AUDITOR-CYCLE-FINDINGS-NOT-SELF-PERSISTED (already READY, next=pm) so its implementation does not ship an incomplete detector.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE / DO NOT DO: (i) do not add another in-flow 'before returning, confirm you made N tool calls' self-check -- that is the exact vacuous reader-is-writer layer this row exists to route around, and it was considered and rejected in this triage; (ii) do not commission a fleet-wide agent-father sweep of all 45 docs/agents/*/flow/main.md files -- per-agent prose hardening is what already failed for market-watcher; (iii) no edits to .claude/agents/*.md (agent-father's zone, not needed for this fix).

items.title: [BCTC-1345b] alert hard-codes 'Check for OCR corruption (VNM/VEA pattern: assets<equity or margin>100%)' but financial=0.10 is emitted ONLY by the unit-mismatch short-circuit that bypasses those rules entirely — 65 live rows (23 tickers) each send the triager to a rule family that provably cannot return 0.10
items.source: telegram_reports id=4273 (from_agent=analysis-agent, 2026-08-01T05:52:16Z, NVL 2026-Q2 composite=0.10 financial=0.10)
items.desc:
MEASURED, not inferred.

ROOT CAUSE. parseBctcReport.ts:737-741 computes confidence_financial as a ternary: when detectUnitMismatch(totalAssets, netRevenue) (cross-statement, >1000x) OR detectBsIntraStmtUnitMismatch(totalAssets, totalLiabilities) (intra-BS, >100x) fires, it SHORT-CIRCUITS to the literal 0.1 and validateFinancialFigures() is never called. The alert built at parseBctcReport.ts:275-279 then tells the reader to check the VNM/VEA patterns -- but those are BCTC-VAL-01 (assets<equity) and BCTC-VAL-03 (margin>100%), both implemented INSIDE the validateFinancialFigures() call that was just skipped.

PROOF THE HINT IS UNREACHABLE FOR THIS VALUE. Brute-forced validateFinancialFigures over 160,000 input combinations (totalAssets/totalEquity/totalLiabilities/netRevenue x 10 values each, operatingMargin x 16): the ONLY outputs it can ever return are {0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}. It returns 0.1 ZERO times. Documented VNM pattern (assets 957 << equity 18829, revenue 63645) -> 0.8; same without the >30x-revenue escape -> 0.0; documented VEA pattern (margin 3.3 = 330%) -> 0.8. None is 0.10. Therefore financial=0.10 is a UNIQUE, unambiguous fingerprint of the unit-mismatch branch and NEVER of the two patterns the alert names.

SECOND DEFECT -- DEAD FLOOR. financialFiguresValidator.ts:306 'return Math.max(confidence, 0.1)' and its docstrings at :28 and :177 ('soft violations stack, floor at 0.1') describe a floor that cannot be reached: max stacked soft penalty is 0.6, because BCTC-VAL-01's guard requires totalEquity>0 while BCTC-VAL-06 requires totalEquity<0, so those two can never both fire. Minimum non-hard-fail output is 0.4. The 0.1 in the docstring is what makes the collision with the unit-mismatch sentinel invisible on reading.

LIVE BLAST RADIUS (market.db via runtime container, 2026-08-01T06:2xZ). confidence_financial distribution over 221 non-null rows: 1.0 -> 121, 0.1 -> 65, 0.8 -> 18, 0.0 -> 17. Note 0.4 and 0.6 have ZERO rows, and 0.1 is the 2nd most common value at 29.4%. All 65 came through the unit-mismatch branch (independently corroborates the brute-force). 23 distinct tickers. Sub-detector split over those 65: cross-statement only 44, intra-BS only 11, both 7, neither-now 3.

TRIGGERING INSTANCE. NVL 2026-Q2, parsed_at 2026-08-01T05:52:14.418Z: total_assets=420322071420, total_liabilities=0, equity_total=0, net_revenue=31, extraction_confidence=0.375, confidence_financial=0.1, validation_status=low_confidence. assets/revenue ratio = 1.4e10 -> detectUnitMismatch fires (raw VND vs trieu VND). assets>equity, so the VNM signature the alert names is ABSENT; the VEA margin rule was never evaluated. Contained at serve time only INCIDENTALLY: get_bctc_full returns 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' via PUB-1 (refine_status=PENDING, not DONE/PARTIAL) -- NOT via any corruption guard. checkBctcIdentityGuard's predicate (total_assets<=0 OR total_assets<equity_total) passes this row, since equity_total=0 makes assets>=equity trivially true.

AC-1: the [BCTC-1345b] message must name the detector that ACTUALLY fired -- cross-statement unit mismatch (assets/revenue ratio R), intra-BS unit mismatch (assets/liabilities ratio R), or the specific BCTC-VAL-NN rule -- with the offending figures. No hard-coded ticker-pattern hint.
AC-2: the VNM/VEA hint may only appear on values that rule family can actually return (0.0/0.8).
AC-3: resolve financialFiguresValidator.ts:306. Either delete the unreachable floor and correct the :28/:177 docstrings, or keep it and move the unit-mismatch sentinel off 0.1 so the two stop colliding. Do NOT silently leave both.
AC-4: regression test asserting the unit-mismatch alert text does NOT contain the VNM/VEA string, and that a genuine BCTC-VAL-01/03 alert does.
AC-5: NON-GOAL -- this row does NOT fix the underlying unit normalisation (no open row owns that; the 2026-06-07 commit 06c65978c added the DETECTOR only) and does NOT repair the 65 existing rows. Scope is alert truthfulness + the dead floor.

PRIOR ART CHECKED. FIX-BCTC-1345B-REPORT-BATCH (review[], next_agent=qa) touches the same emission block but is about VOLUME/dedup, not text correctness -- its verdict must not be read as making this alert accurate. FIX-BCTC-VALIDATION-GATE-NONBANK-ZERO-SCALE (backlog, architect) is the serve-time validation_status label, not the alert. SPIKE-BCTC-CONVICTION-COMPOSITE-DRAG-PERFECT-FINANCIAL is the inverse case (financial=1.00 dragged by extraction). 48 open BCTC rows scanned; none covers this.

items.evidence_20260814: TWO 2026-08-13 instances that are the row's INVERSE and should be read as a scope check before the QA verdict lands. Telegram 4827 (HPG 2025-Q4) and 4828 (VJC 2025-Q1) both carry composite=0.00/financial=0.00 — NOT the financial=0.10 unit-mismatch short-circuit this row is about — and both DO name a concrete triggering rule (4827 BCTC-VAL-01 total_assets=98670778.69 < total_equity=3101380352.22; 4828 BCTC-VAL-10 operating_margin=45970432% beyond the +/-500% bound). So on the 0.00 path the alert's rule citation is ACCURATE and actionable, and only the trailing boilerplate '(matches the VNM/VEA OCR-corruption signature: assets<equity or margin>100%)' is redundant. This row's fix must therefore be scoped to the financial=0.10 path only — a blanket removal of the OCR-corruption sentence would strip a correct citation from the 0.00 path.
items.status_note:
[QA] Direct-Commit Verify FAILED 2026-08-14 — CHANGES_REQUESTED. Commit 7ac55adc8 verified on main ancestry, both claimed files present (git show --stat), targeted regression suite FIX-BCTC-1345B-ALERT-NAMES-A-RULE-FAMILY.test.ts 9/9 pass, bun tsc --noEmit clean, mock-guard PASS. AC-1 (name the real detector, no hard-coded ticker hint) is genuinely met.

AC-2 is NOT met: describeConfidenceFinancialReason's matchesVnmVeaSignature gate (apps/mcp-server/src/domain/services/financial-reports/confidenceFinancialReasonBuilder.ts:73-77) attaches the VNM/VEA corruption-signature phrase whenever ANY fired violation's rule is BCTC-VAL-01/03/10 — it does not check whether that rule fired ALONE, nor whether the resulting confidence actually landed on 0.0/0.8 as AC-2 requires ("the VNM/VEA hint may only appear on values that rule family can actually return (0.0/0.8)"). Reproduced live: figures {totalAssets:1000, totalEquity:500, totalLiabilities:400, operatingMargin:2.0, netRevenue:-1} -> validateFinancialFiguresDetailed returns confidence=0.6 (BCTC-VAL-03 + BCTC-VAL-05 stacked), yet describeConfidenceFinancialReason still appends "(matches the VNM/VEA OCR-corruption signature: assets<equity or margin>100%)" — a value outside the AC-2-mandated {0.0,0.8} set.

The function's own code comment (confidenceFinancialReasonBuilder.ts:31-33: "a lone VAL-03 soft violation yields exactly 0.8 ... falls out of the function's own structure") is factually wrong — refuted by the task's OWN AC-3 test (FIX-BCTC-1345B-ALERT-NAMES-A-RULE-FAMILY.test.ts:342-356), which stacks VAL-01-SCALE+VAL-03+VAL-05 to reach confidence=0.4, proving VAL-03 is not always lone. This is reachable in production: any report with low extraction confidence (composite=min(extraction,financial)<=0.3) whose financial figures trip BCTC-VAL-03 alongside VAL-05/VAL-06/VAL-01-SCALE will ship an alert falsely claiming the VNM/VEA signature at financial=0.4 or 0.6 — the exact class of misleading-hint bug this task exists to close, relocated rather than removed.

AC-4's regression coverage has a matching gap: the existing "does NOT attach VNM/VEA signature" test (FIX-BCTC-1345B-ALERT-NAMES-A-RULE-FAMILY.test.ts:176-200) only exercises BCTC-VAL-05 ALONE, never VAL-03 co-firing with another soft rule, so this defect shipped un-caught.

FIX NEEDED: gate matchesVnmVeaSignature on violations.length===1 (equivalently confidence===0.0||confidence===0.8), not rule-membership alone; add a regression test asserting the hint is absent when BCTC-VAL-03 stacks with a second soft violation (e.g. VAL-05 or VAL-01-SCALE).

Not routing to fixer — no task branch exists (direct-commit row, branch:null). Held: .task_board.qa[] -> .task_board.review[], status QA -> REVIEW, owner/next_agent=dev-mcp-server, redispatch_count 0 -> 1.


[dev-mcp-server] Direct-commit fix, redispatch after QA CHANGES_REQUESTED on 7ac55adc8. Re-gated matchesVnmVeaSignature (confidenceFinancialReasonBuilder.ts) on violations.length===1 (equivalently confidence===0.0||confidence===0.8), not rule-membership alone -- BCTC-VAL-03 is a stacking soft violation (unlike VAL-01/VAL-10, which hard-fail with exactly 1 violation) and can co-fire with VAL-05/VAL-06/VAL-01-SCALE to land confidence on 0.4/0.6, values the VNM/VEA rule family can never produce. Corrected the misleading module docstring that claimed a lone VAL-03 always yields exactly 0.8 with no separate gate needed. Added 2 regression tests matching QA's exact ask: QA's own live repro (VAL-03+VAL-05 stack -> confidence=0.6, hint absent) and a second stack shape (VAL-03+VAL-01-SCALE -> confidence=0.4, hint absent). items.title: notebook-uuid-provenance guard has sat in default mode=warn since 2026-08-05 — it fires, escalates to PO's inbox, and the UUID commits anyway: session 632721c2-... is live in HEAD across 3 notebooks (agent-father.md, dev-team.md, qa.md). Promote to reject, but scrub BEFORE flipping or the flip hard-blocks those 3 agents' next notebook commit
items.desc:
NOT AN OVERSIGHT — A STAGED ROLLOUT WHOSE PROMOTION STEP WAS NEVER TAKEN. scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit:556 reads `mode_uuid="${GIT_NOTEBOOK_UUID_PROVENANCE_MODE:-warn}"`, and :604 (`[ "$rc" -eq 1 ] && [ "$mode_uuid" != "reject" ] && return 0`) converts the failure to a pass in every mode but reject. The hook's own message at :584 states the intended path verbatim: 'set GIT_NOTEBOOK_UUID_PROVENANCE_MODE=reject to hard-enforce once re-validated via scripts/audits/verify-notebook-uuid-provenance-gate.sh'. That validator already exists. Nobody ever ran it and flipped the default, so the guard has been advisory for 10 days.

OBSERVED COST. The guard is not silent — it escalates. One of the 16 durable-inbox envelopes PO triaged on 2026-08-15T07:28Z was this guard's WARN (envelope 3b33e2e7...). So each occurrence consumes a PO triage slot AND lands in HEAD regardless: an escalation treadmill where the detector works, the escalation is delivered, and the defect ships anyway. Confirmed live at HEAD, not merely staged: `git show HEAD:docs/agent-memory/notebooks/agent-father.md` has the full session UUID on lines 12 and 46, and `git grep -lE "session .[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-" HEAD -- docs/agent-memory/notebooks/` returns agent-father.md, dev-team.md AND qa.md. Standing rule it violates: .claude/skills/notebook-write/SKILL.md AC-1 + feedback_agent_commits_session_uuid_into_notebook — a session id is a per-invocation coordination PARAMETER, never authored into a committed file.

AC-1 ORDERING IS THE WHOLE RISK — DO NOT REORDER. Scrub the 3 committed notebooks FIRST, then flip the default. Flipping first converts a noisy-but-harmless WARN into a hard pre-commit failure for the next notebook commit of all three of those agents, at least two of which (agent-father, qa) have a documented history of losing notebook writes to commit-step failures. A guard that strands the fleet's own memory writes is strictly worse than the leak it prevents — same shape as feedback_red_prepush_strands_fleet and feedback_git_sweep_guard_bare_commit_escalates_hard_block. Replace each UUID with a c<NNN> cycle counter or a fixed source label per AC-1; do NOT use the `notebook-uuid-lint-allow:` escape hatch to paper over these three, it exists for genuine short-SHA source labels.

AC-2. Run scripts/audits/verify-notebook-uuid-provenance-gate.sh and record its verdict on this row before flipping — the hook message names it as the explicit precondition, so flipping without it repeats the shipping-a-guard-without-the-dynamic-case mistake this fleet made the same week with the prose-ceiling guard (see FIX-PROSECEILING-SECONDARY-CLAIM-STAMP-FIELDS-MISSING-FROM-STRUCTURAL-EXCLUDE-SET).

AC-3. Flip the DEFAULT at :556 (`:-warn` -> `:-reject`). Do NOT ship this as an env var that CI or a wrapper is expected to set: an enforcement mode that depends on every caller exporting a variable is the same latent no-op the guard is in today.

AC-4. After the flip, sweep for the NEXT producer rather than assuming the 3 known files are the whole set — the guard only inspects ADDED heading lines in staged notebooks, so any agent that writes a UUID into a non-heading line, or into a file outside docs/agent-memory/notebooks/, is still unguarded. Report the residual surface on this row; widening the guard is explicitly out of scope here.

WHY P3. Nothing is blocked and no data is lost — this is provenance hygiene plus recurring PO-inbox noise. It is worth doing because the detector, the validator and the escape hatch are all already built; the only missing step is a one-token default change plus a 3-file scrub.

items.title: FLEET-WIDE PUSH OUTAGE: pre-push size-lint fails orchStateSchema.ts as a new-offender (1784L, header still declares ~1300L), so EVERY push has been blocked since 21:32Z and origin/main is 40 commits behind and growing
items.desc:
The fleet's only push actuator (launchd com.vn-market.fleet-push -> scripts/fleet-worktree-push.sh) has now attempted and FAILED three consecutive pushes (2026-08-22T21:32:54Z ahead=22, 22:03:40Z ahead=31, 22:34:30Z ahead=36; ahead=40 at triage time). Root cause read VERBATIM from the actuator's own log (docs/agent-memory/sessions/fleet-push.log), not inferred from the signal payload — all three runs emit the byte-identical pair:
  `[size-lint] FAIL - 1 offending file(s) (scanned 1409):`
  `apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/orchStateSchema.ts - new-offender (1784L > 120L, no baseline entry, no current justification header)`
  `[pre-push] BLOCKED: doc-shaped check(s) failed`
The pre-push tsc gate PASSES on all three runs; only the doc-shaped size-lint check blocks. MECHANISM (read from scripts/audits/size-lint-justification.sh:83-129, not guessed): the file DOES carry a size-justification header at line 3, but it declares `~1300L`; the checker reads the header from `head -10`, parses the declared number, and applies a +/-10% (min 5L) tolerance -> upper bound 1430L. Actual 1784L > 1430L, so the header is judged NOT CURRENT and the file falls through to the baseline lookup, where it has no entry -> classified `new-offender` -> FAIL. CAUSAL CHAIN, confirmed via git log on the file: orchStateSchema.ts grew past its stale declaration in commits efcb45ad8 + 1897ef6a2 (the sprint-registry dangling-id guard, QA-approved DONE_VERIFIED at 2026-08-22T22:01Z UTC) - i.e. the very fix that closed FIX-SPRINT-REGISTRY-DANGLING-IDS-BREAK-SIGNOFF-AND-JOURNAL-ARCHIVE is what silently armed the fleet-wide push block ~30 minutes earlier. This is a one-line-class fix with a fleet-wide blast radius.

The one sibling size-lint row, FIX-CI-SIZELINT-GETBCTCPENDINGREFINETOOL-BASELINE-TOLERANCE-EXCEEDED (ready[], occ 7), is a DIFFERENT file (getBctcPendingRefineTool.ts, baseline-tolerance-exceeded 605L vs baseline 464L) and a DIFFERENT failure class - per triage-signals.md's file-scoped dedup discipline this is ONE ROW PER DISTINCT FILE, never collapsed. Note the live pre-push log now names orchStateSchema.ts as the SOLE offender (1 of 1409 scanned), so the getBctcPendingRefineTool breach is no longer surfacing on the pre-push plane; that row is unaffected by this one.

items.acceptance: AC-1 `bash scripts/audits/size-lint-justification.sh --check` exits 0 with orchStateSchema.ts no longer in the offender list - either by refreshing the line-3 `size-justification:` declaration to the file's ACTUAL current line count with an honest reason (preferred, 1-line edit), or by splitting the file if 1784L is genuinely unjustifiable. Do NOT add a baseline entry to grandfather it: docs/data/size-lint-baseline.json is regenerated wholesale by --update and a hand-added entry would be silently dropped on the next regeneration. AC-2 a real push lands: `git push origin HEAD:main` succeeds and `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` returns 0 (or the fleet-push actuator's next run logs a success instead of `[fleet-push] ABORT`). AC-3 (the recurrence guard, and the reason this is UNBLOCK not a bare CLEAN) the abort SIGNAL is made actionable: scripts/fleet-worktree-push.sh's push-fail payload currently reads only `detail: git push origin HEAD:main returned non-zero`, which names no cause - an operator cannot act on it without manually tailing the log. Make the emitted payload carry the failing pre-push check's own output line (e.g. the `[size-lint] FAIL` / offending-file line) so the next occurrence is self-diagnosing. AC-4 verify the fix does not depend on the stale-number failure mode recurring: any future growth of a size-justified file re-arms this exact block, so state in the task report whether a CI-side (not just pre-push-side) size-lint job already covers this file - if CI covers it, the same breach should have turned CI red BEFORE it turned the push path red, and its absence from the ci_red stream is itself a finding.
items.non_goals: Not a change to the size-lint checker's tolerance or threshold (the checker behaved exactly as specified). Not a change to the PUSH_THRESHOLD=20 band - that is the separate, already-tracked FIX-FLEET-PUSH-THRESHOLD-20-DESIGNS-IN-A-20-COMMIT-UNPUSHED-WINDOW (backlog, occ 7, next_agent=ops), which covers the ahead<=20 hard-SKIP case; this row covers the ahead>20 push-ATTEMPTED-and-FAILED case, a disjoint condition that row's own title explicitly excludes.

items.title: pdf-extractor drops contended PEK extractions silently: non-blocking Semaphore(1) acquire raises instantly while bctcExtractReconcileJob re-fires a 20-wide batch of 202-fire-and-forget triggers every 30min
items.source: Architect root-cause brief docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-13-fix-pek-extract-semaphore-contention-silent-drop.md (2026-08-13T23:39:24Z), PO-ratified 2026-08-15 after independent source RAW-verification of all 5 links of the causal chain (see the parent row's po_verification_note). Architect explicitly did not mint this row (task-breakdown is PM/PO job); PO minted it directly rather than routing to pm because the brief already carries a complete fix design + test strategy and a further decomposition hop would only add latency to a P0.
items.desc: apps/pdf-extractor/infrastructure/pek_engine_adapter.py:90-92 declares `_extraction_semaphore = threading.Semaphore(1)` and :656 acquires it with `acquire(blocking=False)`, raising SemaphoreContendedError the instant the slot is held. Upstream, apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/financial-reports/bctcExtractReconcileJob.ts (DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=20, loop 420-527) re-fires every still-pek_triggered row back-to-back with no pacing. The per-row `await` does NOT serialize anything: pekExtractTrigger.ts treats HTTP 202 as success and routes_pek.py returns 202 immediately via FastAPI BackgroundTasks — so one tick launches up to 20 CONCURRENT background extractions against a 1-slot semaphore. The 19 losers raise SemaphoreContendedError inside the detached background task, where pek_run_helper.py's bare `except Exception` logs '_run_pek_extract: FAILED' and returns. Nothing requeues, nothing reaches the caller (it already has its 202), and the reconcile job records `refired++` for a request that never ran — burning one of MAX_RECONCILE_ATTEMPTS=8. Net effect: real-UUID reports with a valid pdf_path and text_status=COMPLETE march to reconcile_attempts=8 with 0 rows in bctc_layout_units/bctc_table_rows/bctc_md_tables and terminate as enrich_failed, emitting the RECONCILE EXHAUSTED alerts this SPIKE was opened on (HUT 2025-Q3, BSR 2024-Q1, FRT 2024-Q1). Architect measured 129 of 183 FAILED traces as SemaphoreContendedError and reproduced FRT 2024-Q1 losing 8/8 passes; malformed-PDF was ruled out because BSR/FRT 2025-Q1 filings extracted fine (34/27 layout units) once they won the race. This is NOT the fallback-shell defect — none of these ids is a fallback- shell and none reaches that write gate.
acceptance: AC-1 pek_engine_adapter.py gains an env-configurable wait bound in the same style as the existing _EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: _DEFAULT_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS = 30*60 and _SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get('PEK_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS', _DEFAULT_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS)). Confirm PEK_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SECONDS is genuinely new: PO grepped the repo 2026-08-15 and found zero occurrences, so it must also be plumbed wherever pdf-extractor env is declared (compose/env file) if that is how the sibling PDFX_OCR_QUEUE_WAIT_S is surfaced.

AC-2 extract_layout_and_tables() acquires with `acquire(blocking=True, timeout=wait)` and accepts an optional `wait_s: Optional[float] = None` override (mirrors ocr_gateway.slot(timeout_s=None)) so tests inject a short bound instead of monkeypatching a module constant. SemaphoreContendedError class name and the existing try/finally release stay UNCHANGED — only the message changes (from 'instant reject' to 'waited Ns, still no slot').

AC-3 Reuse only — no new concurrency primitive. The shape is already shipped at apps/pdf-extractor/infrastructure/ocr_gateway.py:140 (_OCR_SLOTS) and :382-383 (_acquire_slot_blocking -> acquire(blocking=True, timeout=timeout_s)). PO verified both exist as described.

AC-4 Stale doc-comment correction (in scope, do not defer): the module docstring at pek_engine_adapter.py:24 and the method docstring at :653 both claim contention maps to 'HTTP 429 at the handler level'. That is FALSE on the real /pek-extract path — routes_pek.py returns 202 before the background task starts and SemaphoreContendedError is swallowed by pek_run_helper.py's except-Exception, never reaching an HTTP response. Rewrite both to describe the actual behavior (bounded wait, then a logged FAILED trace, no HTTP code involved).

AC-5 Tests: MODIFY apps/pdf-extractor/__tests__/test_pek_engine_adapter.py::TestSemaphoreGuard::test_semaphore_contention_raises_error (it currently asserts the IMMEDIATE raise this fix removes) to pass wait_s=0.2 and assert both that it still raises after the bound elapses AND that elapsed wall-clock is close to wait_s, not instant — mirror the `elapsed < 3.0` idiom in test_ocr_concurrency_invariant.py:384-392. KEEP test_semaphore_released_after_extraction as-is.
AC-6 NEW test: a second thread releases the semaphore BEFORE the wait bound elapses -> the waiting call acquires and succeeds instead of raising. Proves this is a real queue, not sleep-then-fail.

AC-7 NEW batch-realistic test: N=3 threads call extract_layout_and_tables concurrently (mocked fast _run_extraction) with wait_s large enough to cover serialized execution -> ALL 3 return successfully, none raises. This is the row's actual real-world claim: a contended batch of re-fires loses no members.

AC-8 Live post-deploy verification (REQUIRED, not optional): after deploy, re-probe bctc_layout_units/bctc_table_rows counts for HUT 2025-Q3 (dab264ae-9702-4045-b488-bbf5d13f97fc), BSR 2024-Q1 (d332bf35-d989-4dcc-a180-48c07369ea01), FRT 2024-Q1 (268f4544-d66b-42cd-b37e-18ff7b17d55f) after their next reconcile pass, and re-check pdf-extractor logs for SemaphoreContendedError falling to ~zero across a 24h window that CONTAINS a live reconcile batch. CAVEAT from PO: these 3 rows are already terminal enrich_failed with reconcile_attempts at/over cap, so the reconcile job will NOT re-select them (it queries status='pek_triggered' only) — AC-8 requires either a deliberate requeue or substituting 3 currently-live pek_triggered rows. Do not report AC-8 PASS on a window with zero extraction traffic; PO hit exactly that false-read (1068 log lines, zero pek-extract requests) on 2026-08-15.

AC-9 Test the A-30 correlation claim empirically over the same window: architect read system-auditor's pdf-extractor sustained-memory signal (telegram 4648, 94.07% loss of reclamation) as a DOWNSTREAM symptom of the same burst (thread-pool churn from N simultaneous asyncio.to_thread calls), not an independent leak — the burst at 12:35:03-04Z preceded the A-30 alert at 12:36:20Z by ~1min. Record whether A-30 quiets post-fix. If it does NOT, say so plainly rather than closing the row silently — that would refute the correlation-not-causation read and needs a follow-up row.

MECHANISM, all three legs RAW-verified 2026-07-30T21:48Z: (leg 1) scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq deps_satisfied() is satisfied only when EVERY dep resolves to the exact string DONE_VERIFIED - its own comment says verbatim 'plain DONE is NOT sufficient'. po_scope_calls_NOT_design: RULED OUT - loosening deps_satisfied() to accept plain DONE. That deletes the distinction the strict token exists to enforce (landed != verified) and would silently auto-dispatch successors of genuinely unverified work. Do not re-scope the gate as the fix (feedback_gate_widening_recommendation_requires_actuator_dry_run) - the gate is correct; the PRODUCER is missing.

RULED OUT as a SOLE fix - another flow-doc line telling agents to remember to write DONE_VERIFIED. 25+ hand-minted one-off jq scripts already prove that vigilance-shaped control does not hold, and this is the same disposition that failed 3x on the commit-pathspec class.

IN SCOPE for architect - WHICH mechanism produces the token, and its failure-safety. Candidates the architect chooses between, not a pre-made decision: (a) a done[]-lane sweeper on the dev-team idle chain, symmetric with the existing Review QA-Drain, that routes a DONE row to its next_agent (qa where set) and lets QA promote the token; (b) making DONE a lane-illegal terminal state so a row must land as DONE_VERIFIED, CANCELLED etc. and any DONE row is loud; (c) both. Whichever is chosen must NOT auto-promote DONE -> DONE_VERIFIED without a verifier - that would make the token vacuous and is strictly worse than the current starvation (feedback_reader_writes_its_own_trigger_field_check_is_vacuous).
items.acceptance: (1) A named, executable producer for the DONE_VERIFIED token exists and is wired into a lane that actually runs (the dev-team idle chain rotation, or an equivalent the architect justifies), so a finished row reaching done[] cannot sit there indefinitely. (2) A DONE row carrying next_agent is REACHED by that producer - demonstrate on the two live 2-day-old cases (TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2, FACTORY-APP-split-assembleBriefing, both next=qa). (3) The producer NEVER promotes DONE -> DONE_VERIFIED on its own authority; promotion requires the verifier the token denotes. A row it cannot verify must become LOUDER (surfaced), not silently promoted. (4) A row that lands in done[] with NO next_agent is not silently invisible - it is surfaced to PO/router rather than defaulting to permanent residence. (5) The 8 currently-starved rows are re-measured with the ACTUAL predicate after the fix; the count must drop, and any row still starved must have a named reason. (6) Regression instrument: a script that re-runs is_bounded1_eligible over backlog[]+ready[] and reports the sole-deps_satisfied-failure set, so this class is detectable next time instead of being re-derived by hand.

items.architect_review_note: Full design: docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-08-donelane-doneverified-producer.md. DECISION: candidate (a) — reuse (extend, not duplicate) the existing Review-Lane QA-Drain + Review-Lane SECONDARY-Drain mechanisms by widening their candidate-gathering from review[] alone to review[] UNION done[] (status REVIEW / DONE respectively). Zero new dev-team/flow/main.md sections, zero new bash call sites, zero new .head coordination — the mechanism inherits the SAME already-reachability-proven idle-chain-rotation + head-decoupled reach as review[] today. QA-routed subset (next_agent==qa) moves into qa[] exactly like a review[]-origin row and is verified/promoted ONLY by QA's own pre-existing, UNMODIFIED verify-committed judgment (producer never self-promotes — AC-3 honored by construction, not by a new check). Non-qa/null subset is stamped in place and dispatched via the pre-existing resolved_secondary_dispatch_target() fallback to po (AC-4 satisfied for free, no PO flow change needed). REJECTED full option (b) (DONE lane-illegal repo-wide): blast radius across every dev-* completion path, for a defect that is 'missing reader' not 'illegal landing state' -- same diagnosis PO's own po_scope_calls_NOT_design already applied one level down to deps_satisfied() itself. ADOPTED a NARROW, high-leverage slice of (b)'s spirit instead (Component 6): exclude status==DONE rows from orch-cold-evict.sh's done[] age/count eviction pass entirely (only DONE_VERIFIED rows in done[] remain evictable) -- closes the exact historical failure mode this cycle's live re-measurement found (FIX-BCTC-TABLE-COLUMN-FPT-OVERFIT / FIX-CYCLEJOB-1294-MACRO-TEST-UNMOCKED-LIVE-FETCH already cold-evicted pre-guard, still at DONE, now permanently unreachable by any hot-file mechanism -- flagged to PO in the brief SS5 as a one-time hand-verify, same treatment as LAYER2, NOT part of this row's scope). BLOCKING CROSS-DEPENDENCY (brief SS3, not introduced by this task): orchStateSchema.ts checkVerificationGate (shipped TODAY by SYSREMAKE-P2-T2-SCHEMA-ADDITIONS) hard-rejects any DONE_VERIFIED write without verification.raw_probe unless grandfathered -- neither demo row is grandfathered (list is frozen/closed), and qa/flow/main.md verify-committed-approved does not yet populate raw_probe (its own flow-doc wiring, SYSREMAKE-P2-T8-FLOW-DOC-WIRING, next_agent=agent-father, is READY but unimplemented). The verification_gate demo WILL hit this wall unless QA hand-constructs a compliant raw_probe from evidence it already collects, or the demo is sequenced after T8 lands -- flag this to whoever runs the demo, a rejected write here is NOT a Done-Lane Drain defect. LIVE RE-MEASUREMENT this cycle (not the 2026-07-30 snapshot): of the original 8 starved rows, 6 are STILL starved today by the pure DONE-not-DONE_VERIFIED class (TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3/4/5, FACTORY-APP-split-assembleEveningSummary, FU-FPT-2025Q4-STAGE4-DUP, FIX-CYCLEJOB-1294-FOLLOWUP-SWEEP-UNMOCKED-LIVE-FETCH); 1 resolved (LAYER2, PO hand-flip); 1 drifted to a mixed cause (FIX-COMMIT-SWEEP-VICTIM-SELF-DETECT, now also blocked on a genuinely MISSING dep). Both named demo rows (TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2, FACTORY-APP-split-assembleBriefing) confirmed still resident in hot done[], NOT hand-flipped, protected from cold-eviction today by the referential-integrity guard (live dependents still name them). Companion row FIX-DONELANE-DEVTEAM-FLOWDOC-PROSE-SYNC (agent-father, docs/agents/dev-team/flow/ + docs/agents/qa/flow/) covers the prose-sync half -- NON-BLOCKING, the mechanism is fully live the moment this row's scripts/ changes land, independent of that row's timing.

items.qa_changes_requested_20260823T1345Z:
[QA] CHANGES_REQUESTED (direct-commit verify, 2026-08-23T13:45Z) - BLOCKING DEFECT, found by EXECUTING the shipped actuator through the real write path rather than reading it. Commit 863a250e3 is real and on main, and AC-3 (self-verify) is fine, but AC-1's block as shipped HARD-REJECTS at orch-apply.sh Stage-1 validation and can never complete a lane move.

BLOCKING ISSUE - docs/agents/qa/flow/main.md:218 (vc-approved jq block, the line 'next_agent: null,'): the done_verified[] lane is validated by Lane -> the task-row schema at apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/orchStateSchema.ts:208, which declares 'next_agent: z.string().optional()' - OPTIONAL (key may be ABSENT) but NOT NULLABLE. Writing an explicit null therefore fails Zod. Reproduced live this cycle on a real 10-row batch: 'ORCH-STATE VALIDATION FAILED (10 issues) ... [1] task_board.done_verified[30].next_agent: expected string, received null' x10, then '[orch-apply] ABORTED: validator exit 2 - live file untouched'. Corroborated by live data: of 30 existing done_verified[] rows, 27 carry a string next_agent and 3 OMIT the key entirely - ZERO carry an explicit null.

ROOT CAUSE (not just the symptom): the block borrowed the '.head' idiom, where 'next_agent: null' IS legal - HeadSchema at orchStateSchema.ts:324 declares 'next_agent: z.string().nullable().optional()'. That nullable spelling was copied into a task-row context governed by the non-nullable :208 spelling.

FIX: replace 'next_agent: null,' with a key deletion, e.g. build the row as '($t + {status:"DONE_VERIFIED", qa_verified_at:$now, status_note:...} | del(.next_agent))' - matching the 3 live rows that omit the key. Do NOT substitute an empty string; :208 would accept it but it is a fake routing value.

SECOND, LATENT INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS - docs/agents/qa/flow/main.md:252 (vc-changes block, 'next_agent: $t.owner'): if the row has no owner (or owner is null) this writes null and fails identically. Not hypothetical - RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND and FIX-PEK-EXTRACT-SEMAPHORE-CONTENTION-BOUNDED-QUEUE both sit in review[] right now with owner absent. Guard it, e.g. 'next_agent: ($t.owner // "po")' or refuse up-front when owner is unresolvable.

THIRD (non-blocking, design gap): both blocks are hard-guarded to source lane qa[] with 'status != "QA" -> refuse'. Every one of the 13 rows in today's QA batch arrived in review[] with status REVIEW, so the actuator refuses on the lane rows actually arrive in and QA still has to hand-adapt (the cycle-809 workaround). The refusal is correct fail-safe behaviour, not a bug, but AC-1/AC-2 do not yet cover the observed dispatch shape.

WHAT PASSES, for the re-fix: the jq transform logic itself is otherwise correct - verified against a fixture, both refuse-guards fire with the right messages, redispatch_count increments 0->1, status_note appends cleanly, and a guard error mid-pipe is safe because orch-apply.sh rejects empty stdin ('empty candidate - aborting'). Only the next_agent typing is wrong. AC-4/AC-5 (scripts/ regression verifier + fixtures) remain correctly out of agent-father zone - QA ENDORSES minting them to a developer: a one-line executable fixture asserting each block's output passes orch-validate.mjs would have caught this before it shipped.

items.qa_changes_requested_20260823T1355Z:
[QA] CHANGES_REQUESTED 2026-08-23T13:54:07Z — RETRACTS the DONE_VERIFIED this same QA cycle issued ~25 min earlier. My first pass verified the REACHABILITY half only (steps 1-3e above the RETURN, 0 invariant violations — that half is genuinely fixed, keep it). A concurrently-running pm agent then executed the shipped Step 3e against 9 real parents and could not use it; I re-tested its report rather than accepting it, and claim 1 HOLDS.

[1] BLOCKER — docs/agents/pm/flow/main.md Step 3e: BOTH jq branches resolve the parent from in_progress[] and active_sprints[].tasks[] ONLY.
  CLOSEOUT branch on a ready[] parent: $row resolves null and jq's 'null + {...}' appends an ID-LESS GHOST ROW to done[] while the parent STAYS in ready[] (reproduced verbatim: done[] gains {status:DONE, closed_at, children} with no id/title/owner; ready[] still holds the parent). orch-validate.mjs then hard-rejects the whole write ('task_board.done[21].id: expected string, received undefined'), so the step is UNUSABLE on such parents — exactly what pm hit, 8 of its 9 parents were in ready[].
  PARTIAL branch on a ready[] parent is WORSE: it fails SILENTLY. Its two map() calls only touch in_progress[] and active_sprints[], so the ready[] parent is left untouched, jq exits 0, orch-apply.sh succeeds, and the '|| echo ABORTED' guard never fires. A no-op that reports success.
  SCOPE IS WIDER THAN pm REPORTED — measured live on the board this cycle, rows carrying children[] (real decomposition parents) sit in: backlog 10, done 9, ready 6, in_progress 1. So ready[] AND backlog[] are both unhandled, while in_progress[] — the one lane the step handles — holds just 1. Dominant case, not an edge case. I flagged this same not-found hazard as 'non-blocking fail-safe' on my first pass and under-sized it; pm's frequency evidence is what makes it blocking.
  FIX: resolve $row across the full non-terminal lane set (backlog/ready/in_progress/active_sprints[].tasks), delete it from whichever lane it was found in, and add an explicit 'if $row == null then error(...)' refuse-guard so a miss fails LOUD instead of producing a ghost row or a silent no-op — mirroring the error("id not in qa[] -- refuse") idiom shipped in docs/agents/qa/flow/main.md the same day.

[2] pm's SECOND claim — that the step writes a schema-invalid 'next_agent: null' — DOES NOT HOLD for this row, recorded rather than passed through. The only 'next_agent: null' in Step 3e is inside the '.head = {...}' object in both branches, and .head is governed by HeadSchema at apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/orchStateSchema.ts:324 ('next_agent: z.string().nullable().optional()') — nullable, therefore LEGAL. The closeout branch builds the parent as '$row + {status, closed_at, children}', preserving the row's existing next_agent; it never nulls it. The genuine non-nullable-task-row defect (schema :208) is real but belongs to FIX-QA-VC-LANEMOVE-PROSE-ONLY-NO-ORCHAPPLY-ACTUATOR, where I confirmed and filed it independently — it appears to have been carried across between the two rows. Do NOT 'fix' a null this file does not write.

KEEP AS-IS on re-fix (all fixture-verified good): the reachability restructure (steps 1/2/3/3b/3c/3d/3e above '## RETURN' :163; steps 4/4b below it under the declared '## Task Lifecycle — Later-Cycle Steps' boundary :175 = 0 violations); the DECOMPOSITION_COMPLETE true/false split; the children[] write; the .head guard (fires only when .head.active_task_id still names $SPRINT_ID, correctly skipped otherwise); and the Step 3 next_agent conditionally-mandatory-at-mint shape note. Only the lane-resolution set and the missing null-guard are wrong.

PO RULING 2026-08-24T14:05Z - the 5-cron '~5h overdue' cluster reported by the tier-2 auditor cycle (vpsProxyWatchdog 5h, priceUpdateWatchdog 5h, vnIndexRefresh 5h, alertScanParallel 5.1h, taAlertNotifier 5.1h) is NOT a cron failure and NOT an outage artifact. It is the normal daily market-hours stand-down, misread by a raw-age ladder - i.e. exactly the defect THIS row already describes ('classifyCronLiveness() ignores the expected_last_fire it already computes and ladders on raw age vs cadence'), now reproduced on a WEEKDAY rather than the weekend case already written up here.

MEASURED IN cron_job_runs (live market.db via `docker exec vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1`, NOT the host data/ copy - the live DB is a named volume):
  vnIndexRefreshJob      last 2026-08-24 08:55:02  n=84
  vpsProxyWatchdogJob    last 2026-08-24 08:50:00  n=42
  alertScanParallelJob   last 2026-08-24 08:45:02  n=28
  taAlertNotifierJob     last 2026-08-24 08:45:02  n=28
Every one of those daily counts is IDENTICAL to 2026-08-12, 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14 (full trading sessions). Every daily envelope is first=02:00 last=08:45/08:50/08:55 UTC = 09:00-15:55 ICT, the VN trading session. 2026-08-24 is a Monday and a completely normal session (2098 fleet cron runs across 64 distinct jobs).

WHY THE DETECTOR IS WRONG: these jobs are market-hours-scoped, so between session close 08:55Z and next open 02:00Z they are ALWAYS 5h-to-17h 'overdue' by raw age vs cadence. The condition is the DESIGNED daily state and it recurs every single day - a permanent daily false-CRITICAL generator, not a weekend-only one. Five 'independent' crons agreeing to within 0.1h is not five deaths and not one outage; it is one shared schedule envelope.

FIFTH NAME IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT: priceUpdateWatchdog has ZERO rows under any %priceUpdate% match in cron_job_runs. That is the A-29b unresolved-join class owned by FIX-CRONSTATUS-STATICMAP-MISSING-9-PAIRS (task_board.backlog[436]) - not a dead cron. Do not chase it here.

DO NOT CONFUSE WITH THE REAL OUTAGE: 2026-08-19/20/21 have no cron rows at all and 08-17/08-18 are truncated (42 and 154 runs vs ~3150 on a normal day). That IS the documented multi-day host suspension - and it ENDED (08-22 1215, 08-23 2589, 08-24 2098-and-climbing). The 2026-08-24 cluster is unrelated to it.

PROVENANCE: recorded here rather than inline because this row is over ORCH_ROW_PROSE_CEILING_BYTES (live 15638B); scripts/orch-apply.sh's row-prose-ceiling check refuses inline growth and names detail_ref as the sanctioned destination.
